areas.summary:
Scope: the bento plugin (source at /home/ketan/project/bento, installed copy 2.3.82) and how it shapes agent behaviour in shatter. I checked it against 113 shatter session transcripts since 2026-09-05, ran bento scripts read-only, and looked at the live state of /tmp, the worktrees, remote branches and the beads hooks. The full narrative is at /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/audit-2026-09-22/audits/2026-09-22/areas/bento.md.

Headline: every 2026-09-04 bento finding was filed and closed (bento-rdtn, 15 of 15). Several of those fixes, though, were only tested in single-session fixtures and fail under shatter's real conditions: many concurrent sessions, one shared primary checkout, work done only in linked worktrees, and slow beads hooks.
- The rdtn.3 stale-preview refusal, together with its "remove them first" hint, led two sessions on 2026-09-20 to delete each other's live previews over and over (this pins down the mechanism behind bento-e583).
- land.py's cleanup deletes the verifier log that rdtn.4 exists to keep, and then reports its path as output_path.
- The doctor's "seen once" state (rdtn.2) is stored per checkout, so every worktree session gets the full nudges again.
- The hook-bypass git guard (rdtn.15) can be bypassed by /usr/bin/git, rtk git, cd-to-primary and git -C, and an agent did bypass it on 09-22.
- The all-cached guard (rdtn.6) does nothing for shatter's hand-written verifier, which also discards all gate output.
- The doctor now detects orphan worktree directories, but nothing removes them: the five named on 09-04 (682 MB) are still there, and closure has no mode for them.

Beads post-checkout, post-merge and pre-push hooks add about 300 s to each worktree creation, preview creation and merge/push. Bento's scripts pay this silently, bento's guard blocks the workaround agents had learned, and the guard points to a reference that says nothing about hooks.

Other gaps:
- The land-work skill is 44.6 KB, contradicts its own no-$(...) rule, and was used for only 9 of 35 landings.
- land.py forces a rebase before every landing even though it verifies the exact merge preview.
- The Stop hook overcounts "unpushed" commits after a rebase (69-72 reported).
- The swarm skill tells the lead to land from inside the teammate's worktree, which is the practice a shatter lesson records as causing collisions.
- Landing never deletes remote branches: 39 merged branches remain on origin.
- There is no defined beads snapshot or remote procedure: `bd sync` no longer exists, the tracked jsonl is 15 days stale, and no Dolt remote is configured.

Strengths worth keeping:
- land.py's per-step timing lines and final JSON; about 15 clean landings with gate evidence in close reasons.
- The push-from-preview route, which removed the diverged-primary hazard.
- `launch-work-bootstrap --claim` works.
- The git guard's error messages are well designed (the problem is coverage, not the messages).
- The doctor always exits 0.
- A well-kept bento tracker.

Main agent-system root causes:
1. No harness tests bento under consumer conditions (concurrency, linked worktrees, slow hooks).
2. Epics close when the code merges, not when the symptom is gone; the shatter memory workarounds are still in force.
3. Warnings are raised with no remediation path.
4. Guidance that crosses repos has no contract checks.

Grades: L1 B-, L2 C, L3 C, L4 C, L5 C, L6 B-, AGENT C-.

Scope: bugshot, storystore, the shatter plugin (shatter-agents), global agent guidance, and the agent-env-doctor dormancy nag. Full evidence is in /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/audit-2026-09-22/audits/2026-09-22/areas/plugins-guidance.md. The bento-internal findings (doctor state is per-worktree, bento's test suite leaks previews, orphan worktree dirs) are in areas/bento.md F8/F9/F10 and are not repeated here.

Main finding: the downstream plugin describes an engine that does not exist. The shatter-diff skill documents `shatter diff [<base-ref>] --staged ...`, and its pre-commit hook example blocks every commit. The real CLI rejects it: `unexpected argument '--staged'`, exit 2. compose-shatter-recipe and run-shatter document `.shatter/recipes` and a `stubs:` config registry, but neither the engine nor run_targets.py implements either one. Both tracker items, sa-tyb and sa-yyt, were closed when the skill text landed. The real engine work (str-81xiw, renamed diff-explore) is still open. No contract test connects the plugin to the CLI. The global guidance that would have caught this (wiring-and-consumption, drift-checks) is effectively never loaded: 0 of 87 top-level shatter sessions and 1 of 166 subagent transcripts ever read any agent-guidance or code-writing-guidance leaf file.

Plugin distribution is stale:
- The shatterproof marketplace has no autoUpdate. The installed shatter plugin is 0.1.1 from 2026-06-18; the source is at 0.1.12, 27 commits ahead.
- storystore has not bumped its version since May. Its installed cache is 128 commits behind.

Why storystore is dormant:
- The 09-06 "adopt" decision (str-qwua7.52) was never executed.
- Its inventory finds zero cli-command surfaces in shatter, because only commander.js is supported and clap/cobra are not.
- The installed copy is stale.
- Its bd tracker is write-blocked by a pending v32->v53 schema migration.

Bugshot:
- The CLI-capture prerequisite (bgs-3tq) is P3 in bugshot, while its shatter dependent is P2.
- The interim skip key that the 09-06 decision required was never set, so the nag continues.

Tracker hygiene:
- bugshot and shatter-agents both have mirrored duplicate-prefix issues (55 bugshot-* copies, some open).
- Several issues still describe work as unshipped although it has shipped (sa-d1b, bento-m4y5, str-qwua7.1).

Memory still stands in for a tracker, and some of it is now false. It says the primary checkout is core.bare=true, but the checkout is fixed. Shatter's resource-etiquette rules sit inside the rtk tool-managed marker block. rtk still displays wrong content for `head -5` in compound commands.

Positives:
- shatter-agents' catalog->generated build uses a content-hash auto-bump and a CI clean check.
- The sa-* bugs filed 09-13 are exemplary.
- Within 10 days the bento doctor implemented every repo-state check the 09-04 audit recommended.
- The dotfiles issues from that audit were closed within 72 h, and the rtk prefilter has tests.
- Bugshot's version-bump discipline keeps its installed cache current.
- bgs-3tq is well specified.

Grades: L1 B- (plugin scripts are tidy; parallel discovery logic), L2 D (skills document nonexistent commands), L3 C (guidance index is well factored but unreachable, uses relative paths; shatter-agents CLAUDE.md does not import its rules), L4 C (the plugin duplicates engine discovery and doctor; storystore extractors are TS-only), L5 D+ (storystore and bugshot deliver nothing in shatter, and the shatter plugin misleads downstream users), L6 C (generated CI workflow and wrapper commands fail on first run), AGENT D+ (closure on doc landing, no cross-repo contract checks, unloaded rules, stale memory, and decisions not executed).

Programmatic retrospective of 212 Claude Code transcripts (>=5 KB) across all ~/.claude/projects/*shatter* dirs (2026-08-16 to 09-22), focused on the 89 sessions since the prior audit (09-04 onward). Scripts and outputs are in /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/audit-2026-09-22/audits/2026-09-22/sessions/ (extract.py, aggregate.py, conventions.py, durations.py, humans.py, ngrams.py, errclasses.py and others). The narrative is in audits/2026-09-22/areas/sessions.md.

What improved since 09-04: the tool error rate is low and steady (3.4% of 5,858 calls). No identical failing command repeats 3 or more times in a session (there were 9 such cases before). bento's land.py single-driver landing (a prior-audit recommendation) is in use, and the manual 10-step landing sequence dropped from 49 to 14 occurrences. The bento git guard correctly blocked raw merge, rebase and --no-verify in the primary checkout, and there were zero successful edits into the primary checkout. The swarm-verify traceback was fixed. bd latency is fixed (median 0-1 s). The primary checkout is no longer bare, and main equals origin/main. Agents routinely use code-review, pre-completion and cross-check.

Main new problems:
(1) Busy-wait polling. 820 sleep/echo no-op calls plus 600 ReadNotifications polls, and about 1,078 'Still waiting' turns. In one Sonnet-5 session, 77% of 1,575 tool calls were waits, with 934M cache-read tokens.
(2) The bento hook-bypass guard is trivially evaded. /usr/bin/git, timeout, rtk and env prefixes all get past it (reproduced). One session used /usr/bin/git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null for 13 commits and pushes after the guard shipped.
(3) A shatter memory still instructs agents to use --no-verify. It was reinforced on 09-07, and agents cite it verbatim as their justification.
(4) The pre-commit hook runs the full shatter-core test suite: median 60 s per commit, fragile in fresh worktrees and under load. This is the proximate motivator of the bypasses. Together with the pre-push task affected and the land verifier, it makes a triple gate, and landings take a median of 13 minutes.
(5) The beads post-checkout hook times out at 300 s during landing previews, adding about 4-5 minutes to each landing.
(6) Concurrent sessions overload the machine (load 141-174 on 32 cores) and collide on /tmp. Tests leak 6 GB of /tmp dirs.
(7) The tracker and memories lag reality: bare-primary and push-main issues are open although fixed, str-mpgg1 is in_progress although merged, and the memory still says the primary is bare.

Human input is sparse: 25 genuine messages since 09-04. Corrections were high-signal, for example 'the tests shouldn't be using a globally visible directory like that'. Agents recommended hook bypass as the '(Recommended)' AskUserQuestion option, and the user declined it.

Unverified: a claim in 9f13ca23 that scm tests fail only inside the pre-commit hook environment on 09-19. My repro, run with GIT_INDEX_FILE set, did not finish because of machine load, so it is not reported as a finding.

Grades for the agent system: instructions and memory C- (a stale memory contradicts AGENTS.md and the hooks), hooks and guards C+ (the right intent, but bypassable and noisy), gates and landing C (correct but slow and triple-run), tracker hygiene C, agent behaviour C (waiting and bypass habits), tooling reliability B.

Documentation area review (L2, L3, plus the agent-system causes). Full narrative, tables and repro commands: /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/audit-2026-09-22/audits/2026-09-22/areas/docs.md

Since the 2026-09-04 audit, the P1 first-run items were fixed properly. QUICKSTART and README now work under default-deny. SPEC now documents `--allow-host-writes` and the sandbox policy. The §3.6 and §5.5 examples now deserialize. docs-smoke now runs a real target and deserializes typed YAML/JSON blocks into the real structs.

SPEC flag coverage is close to complete. A scripted check against `--help` found all 220 per-command flags and all 12 global flags mentioned. Only `doctor -d` and `list-targets --scope` are missing from their own sections, and the documented defaults match. Link hygiene is excellent: 0 broken relative links or anchors across 114 tracked `.md` files.

These strengths are worth keeping. The weak spots are in three places:

**(a) Behavior and artifact contracts, beyond flag names.**
- The recommended `SHATTER_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker` remedy (README, QUICKSTART, SPEC, the refusal message) only affects the Go frontend. For TS and Rust targets it also turns off the throwaway-directory guard. Reproduced: a TS target wrote files into the invoking directory.
- `shatter diff` is documented as the snapshot-regression workflow, but no command produces a snapshot file. Every JSON the CLI writes is rejected with exit 2.
- The producers and consumers of spec files disagree. `compare` rejects the `--spec-out` bundle.
- SPEC §5.1 shows an obsolete default report format.
- SPEC §6.1 and §6.2 are stale. The progress fields changed, and one scan's files are split across a 16-hex checkpoint directory and a 64-hex artifact directory.

**(b) Changelog and section drift.**
- The backfilled SPEC changelog rows say §2.8, §2.9 and §3.6 were updated, but those sections were never edited.
- The 09-14 and 09-19 changes have no rows.
- `--failure-threshold` still appears in §2.11 even though the flag does not exist.

**(c) Information architecture, with no progress.**
- The work tracked as str-qwua7.21, .44, .45, .46 and .52 (config reference, status banners and orphans, stale PARITY and CI docs, doc lint, stories) has not moved.
- Orphan docs grew to about 40, and a new 1,695-line plan landed in the duplicate `docs/superpowers/plans` tree.
- `docs/stories` is still absent 16 days after the "adopt storystore" decision.

**Agent-system causes:**
- Neither CLAUDE.md's completion checklist nor `/pre-completion` asks for SPEC, QUICKSTART or changelog updates.
- The mechanical CLI-surface gate (str-wurp) has been open for three months.
- The superpowers plan-path default is not overridden in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.
- The committed `.beads/issues.jsonl` is 15 days stale. CI drift-patrol reads it, so it shows fixed doc issues as open.
- The 09-04 audit report and evidence sit on an unpushed local branch, yet 68 open issues cite paths from it.
- The shatter-agents plugin never mentions the default-deny policy. Its wrapper convention (also in the README) runs bare `shatter`, which exits 2. The installed plugin cache is 0.1.1, while the source repo says 0.1.10.

Grades: L2 C (flags B+, behavior and artifacts D); L3 C- (clear prose and good entry docs, but weak architecture, no config reference and no stories); AGENT D+.

grades.L5: C (docs-visible workflows: diff unusable, compare/spec-out mismatch)
grades.L6: C+ (help leaks tracker IDs, implicit-init noise on stdout)

areas.summary:
Evidence file: /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/audit-2026-09-22/audits/2026-09-22/areas/tests-ci.md

Headline: CI has been green since 2026-08-30 without running any product test suite, and every other workflow is red with nobody noticing.

- **Why CI is hollow (T-01).** The meta unit test `scripts/test_affected_gates.py:203-212` runs `task --list-all --json` in the repo root. Computing the `up_to_date` field makes go-task write a fresh checksum for every task that has `sources:`. Stage 1 of `task check` runs meta, so stages 2 and 3 then report "is up to date" for core:test-ignored, cli:test, ts:test, go:test, rust-fe:test, rust-rt:test, parity and conformance. I reproduced this in a scratch Taskfile: the tests never execute, not even after a source edit. Adding `--dry`, or dropping `--json`, avoids the checksum writes.
- **CI and local evidence.** In the latest CI log, `task check` takes 78 s, and the only `test result:` lines come from the separate shatter-llm step. CI duration fell from 6–11 min to 3–4 min on 2026-08-30. That was the day after str-35vtk.8 (the list test) and str-35vtk.21 (folding CI into `task check`) landed. Locally, the median successful `check` fell from 286 s to 59 s (gate-times.csv).
- **This explains an open P1.** It is the root cause of str-qwua7.3, which the prior audit filed but could not explain.

Other P1s:
- **No releases (T-02).** Build and Release has failed all 266 of its runs. Windows fails on z3.h and aarch64 on openssl-sys. `gh release list` is empty, so `install.sh` and `action.yml` have nothing to install.
- **Red workflows go unnoticed (T-03).** Drift Patrol fails at Setup Go because it points at a root go.mod that has never existed, yet str-u394l.1 was closed on self-test evidence. Perf CI (its gauntlet step fails, with no reason shown), Devcontainer CI and Docker Image never succeed. No agent workflow or skill checks GitHub Actions results.
- **Cache inputs are incomplete (T-04).** Task `sources:` leave out real inputs: CLI tests/, askama templates, build.rs, and the embedded frontends. core:test-ignored runs all three E2E suites but does not list any frontend source, so a frontend-only change skips E2E.

P2s:
- **affected-gates (T-05)** sends askama `.md` templates to `docs` only. It never selects `docs-smoke`, and core changes never select `cli:test`.
- **Verifier vs CI (T-06)** still differ: the verifier runs no TS, Go or rust-fe tests and discards all output. A Go fix (str-qwua7.4) was closed citing test-standard, which runs no Go tests.
- **Runners (T-07).** Locally tests run under nextest; CI uses plain `cargo test`. The nextest `ci` profile is never used, and the flake-serialization group only applies under nextest.
- **Snapshots (T-08).** Snapshot helpers write a missing snapshot and pass. There are four copy-pasted helpers, whitespace-collapsed HTML comparison, and no CLI terminal-output snapshots.
- **Unpinned examples (T-09).** The examples repo floats on `origin/main`, so test results are not reproducible.
- **Dead wiring (T-10).** About 220 script unit tests, plus gate-receipt, gate-event-log and gate-pressure, are not reachable from any gate.
- **No end-to-end CI (T-11).** Smoke, walkthrough and gauntlet never run in CI.
- **Weak TS property tests (T-12).** They are mostly JSON round-trips; the instrumentor and analyzer have none.
- **Too many tiers (T-13).** About 20 overlapping tiers, with four task bodies copied only to get separate cache keys.

**Grades:**

| Level | Grade | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | B- | Good script tests; snapshot and PBT gaps |
| L4 | D | Cached gates and hollow CI |
| AGENT | D | No CI feedback loop; closures accept irrelevant gate evidence; prior P1s unexplored for 17 days |

**Prior audit follow-up:** .2 is still absent; .3 is now explained; .46 and .55 are unchanged; .4 is only partly done (failfile still tracked); .1 looks fixed (`core.bare` is now false) but is still open.

**Positives to keep:**
- gate-wrapper.sh: semaphore, re-entrancy and telemetry.
- affected-gates falls back to the full `check` on unknown paths.
- Structural wiring tests.
- Known-answer E2E design.
- Go rapid package partitioning.

**Urgent:** do not trust any green result since 2026-08-30. The gates agent's forced run is the first real signal in three weeks.

The agent system inside shatter is failing at follow-through. The prior audit is the clearest case. bento acted on all 15 of its items and dotfiles on all 6, within about 3 days. Shatter's own epic str-qwua7 has 12 of 77 items closed. Of its 10 agent-system items, 1 is closed (delete .claude/agents).

Causes, all with evidence below:
- **The only scheduled forcing function never ran.** The Drift Patrol CI job has failed all 7 scheduled runs since 08-10. drift-patrol.yml:85 points setup-go at a nonexistent root go.mod.
- **The audit report was never published.** Branch audit-2026-09-04 was never pushed or merged. All 62 child issues cite files that exist only on that local branch.
- **Priority inflation.** There are 45 open P1s and 154 ready issues. The agent-system items were filed P2 and none was touched, while a new feature epic (str-hjrnp) was started and closed on 09-21/22.
- **Tracker state lags reality.** str-qwua7.1, .18 and .19 are mostly resolved but still open; str-mpgg1 landed on 09-02 and is still in_progress; 7 issues closed since 09-14 carry the bare reason "Closed". AGENTS.md mandates `bd sync`, a command bd 1.1.0 no longer has, and the tracked JSONL is 15 days stale.
- **Two decisions conflict with nothing to resolve them.** The .28 hook-timeout fix contradicts the str-mpgg1 revert. Meanwhile bd post-checkout takes 2m59s per checkout, and memory still tells agents to use --no-verify (43 uses since 09-04).
- **Bento's fixes are opt-in and shatter never adopted them.** The verifier `executed` flag and timeout, log capture, and doctor decision keys all exist in bento. land_work_verifier.sh still discards its output and emits no executed flag.

New problems the prior audit missed:
- The repo's .git/config has user.name=Test / test@example.com, residue of the fixture leak. All of the last 300 commits pushed to GitHub are authored "Test".
- Build and Release has 0 successes in 200 runs and there is no issue for it.
- A global gitignore ignores .claude/ and .codex/, so new skills, and the decided .codex/AGENTS.md, would be silently left untracked.
- The RTK-managed marker block in AGENTS.md swallowed the Shared-Machine Resource Etiquette section, so an rtk re-sync will delete it.
- A 09-07 fixture corruption ("init" commit e50fc399) was never tracked, and str-qwua7.14 was closed as "not reproducible" against that corrupted commit.
- The frontend-parity skill contradicts parity-matrix.yaml (Go thrown_error).
- .claude/swarm-config.md is in a format bento swarm no longer reads.
- 37 merged remote branches were never deleted.

Positives to keep:
- Every task, script and path reference in the agent docs resolves (97 tasks), so the drift lint (str-u394l.4) would be cheap to add as a gate.
- drift-patrol.py itself is well designed: PENDING checks linked to issues, and paste-ready remediation.
- str-jttrf fixed the fixture leak test-first.
- Landings through land.py since 09-19 carry gate evidence in their close reasons.
- The root CLAUDE.md's parallel-path names are accurate.

Full narrative: /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/audit-2026-09-22/audits/2026-09-22/areas/agent-repo.md

shatter-ts has good type discipline: strict tsconfig with noUncheckedIndexedAccess, a clean `tsc --noEmit`, and zero `no-explicit-any` hits when typescript-eslint recommendedTypeChecked runs on production code. Protocol enums are generated, and the adapter architecture in runtime-hooks.ts (ResolverAdapter, SandboxProvider and InvocationHook, all picked from the ExecutionProfile by id) is clean. Other strengths: str-26fhi shares one instrumented sandbox between the direct and adapter paths, fs-write-redirect is thorough, and fast-check is used for real (76 asserts in property.test.ts plus 6 other files).

No TS production code has changed since the 2026-09-04 audit (only two test files), so every prior TS finding still holds: no ESLint (str-qwua7.31), SymExpr builder triplication (str-rf2v), stale CLAUDE.md claims (str-qwua7.24/.25/.34), and missing plan types (str-mhinv.2).

This review found two P1 correctness bugs in the core symbolic path that the prior audit missed. Both were confirmed by driving the real frontend and by probe scripts.
1. The instrumentor's data-flow map ignores where in the function a branch is. It uses the end-of-function state for every branch, never drops a variable's old value when it is reassigned from an unresolvable call, and never widens loops. As a result it emits path constraints that contradict the concrete run. Example: execute of `stale` with inputs [5, 0] reports a branch as taken under `b > 0`.
2. Analyze reports switch, ternary and value-position `&&`/`||` branches, but the instrumentor never records them, and the two passes number branches independently. The core's coverage_metrics joins them by id, so coverage and uncovered-target hints land on the wrong lines. Closed issues str-w0d.1 and str-sunh claimed this was handled.

Further new findings:
- A fourth copy of the SSA flow walker in executor.ts (loop snapshots) has already diverged.
- The TS analyze path ignores data flow, while the parity matrix says TS produces ite.
- The analyzer resolves a shadowed callback parameter to the outer parameter.
- A target error whose message mentions "timeout" is reported as outcome timed_out with category infrastructure.
- The async timeout race leaks a timer on every run, and jest forceExit hides it.
- Requests are validated only at the envelope level, so a bare execute returns internal_error "Cannot read properties of undefined".
- get_invocation_plan returns invalid_request, not the not_supported response CLAUDE.md promises.
- The protocol round-trip tests just check JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x)) and never touch protocol/schemas, although the Taskfile lists schemas and fixtures as test sources.
- The builder-parity property test cannot detect new drift.
- Preflight fails dependency-free projects, and one failure blocks every later request.
- Minor: two lockfiles, a bundle that does not run on its own, and in-flight responses dropped on stdin EOF.

On the agent side, the problems persist because:
- The parity contract talks about AST node-type coverage, not constraint correctness.
- No test checks that a recorded constraint, evaluated on the concrete inputs, matches whether the branch was taken. The core already has triage::evaluate_constraint, which could do this check.
- There is no known-answer e2e test for each branch type.
- Test workarounds, such as the enum e2e reading raw_results, are recorded in CLAUDE.md prose instead of being filed as issues.

Grades: L1 C+, L2 C, L4 B-. Full evidence is in /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/audit-2026-09-22/audits/2026-09-22/areas/frontend-ts.md.

Scope: shatter-rust, shatter-rust-runtime and shatter-llm, reviewed at L1, L2 and L4, with L5 and AGENT observations where evidence came up. The full narrative is in /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/audit-2026-09-22/audits/2026-09-22/areas/frontend-rust.md.

What I checked:
- Read the code and docs directly.
- Ran the shatter-rust frontend over its stdio protocol on probe files.
- Ran `shatter explore --concolic` on small probe crates.
- Built the shatter-rust tests (`--no-run`) and listed the test binaries.
- Checked `select_gates()` in scripts/affected-gates.py.

Status of the 2026-09-04 audit items:
- executor.rs has not changed at all: still exactly 16,125 lines.
- str-qwua7.36 (hand-formatted runtime constraint JSON) is still open, and the problem is worse than the issue describes. The hand-rolled encoder writes invalid JSON for float literals like `1.` and for strings containing control characters. The runtime then silently records those constraints as `unknown`.
- str-qwua7.50 (poison-tolerant locks) rests on a false premise. There is no panic boundary, so any panic already ends the process.
- str-qwua7.43 said to remove the core→shatter-llm dev-dependency cycle. Yesterday's Jev benchmark work made it deeper instead.
- str-qwua7.60 (embed the Rust frontend) has not moved.

New findings from live probes:
- **Crate-bridge stdout collision (P1).** Crate-bridge is the automatic fallback harness for files inside a crate. It writes its JSON result to the same stdout the user's code prints to. Any function that calls `println!` fails with `internal_error: output parse error` (reproduced).
- **Match-arm constraints (P2).** Every match arm is encoded at runtime as a string comparison against the pattern's source text: "0", "1 ..= 5", "k", "_". The analyzer's static condition for a guarded binding arm is also wrong (`n == "k"`).
- **Coverage impact.** A probe with arithmetic, a string with a control character and a 4-arm int match reached only 3 of 7 outcomes in 60 concolic iterations, even though the per-function batch line claimed 5/7 branches.

Design and agent-system findings:
- Timeout budgets are inverted: the CLI request timeout (30 s) is no longer than the build timeout (30 s from the CLI, 120 s as the frontend's own default). A cold Rust build therefore shows up only as a generic "request timed out".
- `main.rs` re-declares the whole module tree, so all 587 inline tests run twice.
- The gate cache and the affected-gates selector miss the runtime crate, `tests/`, and shatter-llm. `task affected` never runs shatter-llm's tests.
- 38 test sites print "skipping" and pass when cargo cannot reach the network.
- The tracker has blank or stale duplicates: str-1fik, str-wfd2 and str-uj3y.
- A stale auto-memory note tells agents the analyzer is single-file. Same-crate cross-file resolution landed in str-do53.
- The Rust CLAUDE.md and parity matrix are wrong on several points: the Tokio runtime flavor, single-file limits, handler line references, console capture, and the timeout table.

shatter-llm: a well-bounded plugin. The traits live in core and the HTTP adapters live in the plugin, with a rate-limit wrapper and a registry. The SeedOracle adapters are reachable from the CLI via `--llm`. Jev, the replay wrapper and the frontier ranker are used only by the benchmark. It has about 82 tests, which run only in CI. Weak points:
- Integer width is not validated.
- The retry backoff has no cap.
- The Jev API key is reachable through derived Debug.
- There is no user documentation.

Strengths worth keeping:
- Non-test frontend code rarely panics, and errors map to typed outcomes.
- The crate-bridge whole-file-then-single-function fallback, with its negative cache, is careful.
- The same-crate type registry is conservative: ambiguous names are dropped rather than guessed.
- The enum value-domain contract states a clear "never guess" invariant.
- codegen_parity.rs pins the hand-written protocol constants to the generated ones.

**Overall assessment.** The engine is ambitious and well documented. Deadline handling, frontend taint-on-timeout, the input-repair funnel and enum-domain solving are careful work.

The central concolic promise breaks on a trivial float program. The Z3 translation declares a separate Int variable and Real variable for the same parameter, and model extraction lets one silently overwrite the other. - **Float probe:** in the random engine, the probe marks paths as seen without counting them, so reports say "0 path(s)" while the progress line says 2.
- **What counts as a path:** the two engines define it differently. Concolic counts 16 paths for a loop with 2 behaviours.
- **Refine phase:** drops `prepare_id` and `execution_profile`, and discards paths it reaches.
- **Shrinker:** there are two value shrinkers. Three fixes (str-ddxe, str-55ep, tuples) landed in the dead copy in input_gen. Open issue str-v0yjq targets the dead copy too.

**Three P1 problems, all new, none in the tracker:**
1. **Installed binaries cannot run uncached Go targets.** The frontend finds its harness runtime module by the source path it was compiled at (`runtime.Caller(0)` in instrument/executor.go:112). The release workflow and shatter-cli/build.rs build without embedding that module, so on a user machine every uncached execute fails. The failure is also mislabelled `build_failed` ("go build failed during harness compilation"). Reproduced with the relocated build.
2. **The documented Go tool install path does not resolve.** `docs/distribution.md` says `go get -tool github.com/shatterproof-ai/shatter/go-tool/...`, but the module lives in `shatter-go-tool/`. Running the command gives "does not contain package". str-fl9g.2 was closed on exactly this acceptance check.
3. **Literal handling in the SymExpr builders is wrong.**
   - Rune/char literals become `const str` in both builders, so `c == 'x'` can never be reached in either explorer mode.
   - The analyzer's `strings.Trim` leaves escapes like `\t` unconverted and strips quote characters that belong to the value.

**Other findings:**
- There are four SymExpr builders, not two:
  - The runtime (instrument) builder never uses its flow map.
  - instrument/flow.go and flowwalk.go are unreachable, even though CLAUDE.md names them as the `ite` mechanism.
  - A fourth builder in loop_body_states resolves parameters and flow values in the opposite order to the analyzer.
- golangci-lint is configured, and the go-conventions skill calls it "Tool-Verified", but no gate or CI job runs it.
  - The partial run reported 10 issues, including 7 unused functions and a tautological `err == nil` check.
  - 9 non-testdata files are not gofmt-clean.

- The upward `.shatter/config.yaml` search has no stop point.
  - A stray /tmp/.shatter/config.yaml is the likely cause of str-k7czv (inferred from the code path; the test run itself was killed under load).
  - An ancestor config can also silently grant `policy.allow`.
- The CLI's `--build-timeout` (SHATTER_BUILD_TIMEOUT) and SHATTER_HARNESS_RELEASE are ignored by Go. Go's `go build` calls have no timeout at all.
- CLAUDE.md has about 10 false or dangling claims, including tracker IDs str-8v66 and str-ruw0 that do not exist.
- shatter-go-tool has robustness gaps:

- Gates check exit codes, artifact integrity and allowlists, not results. Nothing asserts known answers. The gauntlet allowlist of 17 permanent failures has not changed since May and has no ratchet.
- Issues are closed with the bare reason "Closed" (str-6k6.1, str-ior1), so half-built features look finished.
- The coverage goals live only in agent memory files.
- The CLAUDE.md warning about explore/scan parity has no mechanical check. The Go build warmup gate exists only in scan, and at default parallelism under load all 48 Go example functions timed out in explore.
- The shatter-agents plugin ships a shatter-diff skill for a `shatter diff <base-ref> --staged` command that does not exist.

I ran every requested gate in /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/audit-2026-09-22 at 16794cef. Full logs are in /home/ketan/.local/share/worktrees/shatter/audit-2026-09-22/audits/2026-09-22/gates/*.log. The harness blocked writing SUMMARY.md, so the summary is below. Machine load was very high because other audit agents were running at the same time (start load 64, peak about 190 on 32 cores), so treat wall times as upper bounds.

HEADLINE: `task check` exited 0 in a fresh worktree while skipping every stage-2 and stage-3 test, and CI does the same. Root cause, confirmed: the `meta` stage of check-static runs scripts/test_affected_gates.py::test_every_emitted_gate_is_a_real_task, which calls `task --list-all --json` with cwd=ROOT. On go-task 3.50.0 (local) and 3.53.1 (CI), that JSON listing writes .task/checksum files for all 39 tasks that have `sources:`. Once those files exist, rust-rt:test, go:test, go:vet, ts:test, cli:test, rust-fe:test, core:test-ignored (which includes the e2e superset), conformance and parity all report "is up to date" and are skipped. It reproduces in a git-archive copy: plain `task --list`/`--list-all` write 0 checksums, while `--list-all --json` writes 39. CI run 35756993223 shows the same up-to-date lines, and CI wall time fell from about 300–650 s to about 185 s after b12e3054 (str-35vtk.8, 2026-08-29), so CI has probably been hollow since then. This is the root cause behind the open P1 str-qwua7.3, which asks why tasks report "up to date".

Once I deleted .task and ran the stages directly, real failures appeared. check-unit failed (1558 s): go:test TestLoad_MissingFile_ReturnsZeroFile failed deterministically, and ts handlers.test.ts had 10 jest 30 s timeouts that were load-induced (it passed in 28 s on rerun). check-integration failed (472 s): the benchmark bench_frontier_ranking timed out at 120 s in both runs, and fail-fast left 87 of 3531 core tests unrun. With --no-fail-fast, 3530 of 3531 passed. cli:test passed (632), rust-fe:test passed (1178, 2 leaky), rust-rt passed (25). Also passing: e2e (26/23/13, 193 s), smoke (17 s), walkthrough (54 s), gauntlet (314 s, all steps passed, no step-19 timeout this time), parity (2 s), conformance (6 s, but 8 of 18 cases have no cross-frontend check and the '4 frontends x 18 cases = 42 checks' line is arithmetically wrong), workspace clippy, go vet, and tsc --noEmit. drift-patrol failed: tracker-hygiene found 2 stale in_progress issues (str-8q1b4, str-mpgg1) and 4 orphaned children, and it reports docs/stories as nonexistent (PENDING, str-u394l.3). The user asked me to look at docs/stories; that directory does not exist.

The Go failure is environmental but real. An implicit `shatter init` run in /tmp at 11:40 left /tmp/.shatter/config.yaml. The Go loader's findConfigFile walks up to / and so picks that file up from t.TempDir(). The loader's knownTopLevelKeys also omits `defaults`, which `shatter init` itself generates. The test passes with TMPDIR outside /tmp. This is the root cause for str-k7czv.

Tier-table mismatches with CLAUDE.md: (1) CLAUDE.md claims Full/`task check` is the gate for 'Landing, CI' and that CI verifies snapshots, but both are hollow. (2) Standard ('before committing') runs no frontend unit tests. (3) `task check` and `affected` do not cover shatter-llm; CI patches this separately (str-35vtk.36). (4) In `affected`, *.md maps only to `docs`, which is file-existence checks plus linters that are all skipped, and never to `docs-smoke`. (5) `e2e` duplicates work `check` already does. (6) The nextest [profile.ci] is dead config because CI installs no cargo-nextest. (7) A stale 'pending str-7jgm.2' fallback remains in parity-governed. (8) semgrep, markdownlint, vale and lychee are skipped both locally and in CI.

The historical gate-times CSV (since 2026-08-10) shows high non-zero exit rates: affected 28% (44/156), check-fast 24%, check 16%. The median `check` is 129 s against a cold cost of about 1600 s or more, which means most recorded 'passes' executed little.

Strengths: the gate-wrapper/semaphore governance, the timing CSV, docs-smoke, the drift-patrol design (it degrades to SKIP or PENDING instead of a hollow pass, and prints the responsible issue), and gauntlet/walkthrough, which were solid and self-reporting.

findings.title: Leftover-preview refusal and its 'remove them first' hint make concurrent landers delete each other's live previews
findings.evidence: leftover_preview_worktrees() treats every registered land-work-preview-* as a leftover, with no owner, PID or lock check, and the error tells the agent to run --cleanup. land.py never passes --allow-existing. Shatter transcripts, 2026-09-20: at 23:49 session 87606e10 got create_preview failed ('leftover ... /tmp/land-work-preview-mz7t9g27'). git status there showed 'All conflicts fixed but you are still merging', i.e. live. It ran --cleanup, and session 9f13ca23, whose preview it was, then got 'verify: failed (238.362s) ... cleanup: failed'. The reverse happened at 23:54-23:55 (d1bfx2yj, g663hhnu, with rm -rf). At 00:00 87606e10 got create_preview failed after 300.5s: FileNotFoundError on its own /tmp/land-work-preview-2vu7job9.
findings.recommendation: Write an owner lockfile (pid, session, start time) into each preview and hold an flock for the whole land.py run. The leftover check should skip previews that are locked or whose PID is alive, and should say 'another landing is in progress; wait', not 'remove'. --cleanup should refuse previews it does not own unless --force-foreign is given. Add a two-process regression test.
findings.agent_root_cause: rdtn.3 was validated only in single-session fixtures. There is no concurrent-consumer test harness, and the remediation hint was written without considering a live owner.

verify.note: Code claims confirmed in bento 76e45fe: leftover_preview_worktrees (create-preview.py:62-81) flags every registered land-work-preview-* with no owner, PID or lock check. The error at :266-276 says 'remove them first (... --cleanup ...)', and land.py:291 never passes --allow-existing. Transcript 87606e10 contains the 'leftover ... /tmp/land-work-preview-mz7t9g27; remove them first' error. Transcript 9f13ca23 shows 'verify: failed (238.362s) / cleanup: failed'. This is NOT a new issue: open P1 bento-e583 ('preview worktree destroyed mid-verification by concurrent session') already covers the symptom, and its mechanism section is marked unconfirmed. File this as the confirmed-mechanism addendum and recommendation on bento-e583, not as a separate issue. The recommendation (owner lock, liveness check, reworded hint) is sound.

dedupe.note: bento-e583 (open, filed 2026-09-20 from kapow) reports the same symptom: another session destroys a live land-work-preview-* mid-verification. It proposes a pidfile/flock owner lock but leaves the mechanism 'not confirmed'. This finding supplies the root cause: the leftover refusal and 'remove them first' hint added by rdtn.3 (closed) send agents to delete the other lander's live preview. Add this cause, the --force-foreign rule and the two-process test to bento-e583 rather than filing a new issue. bento-nmmk (open) asks for the same kind of flock on the persistent integration_worktree, so one locking design could cover both.

findings.title: land.py deletes the verifier log it reports as output_path on failure
findings.evidence: land.py calls run-verifier without --log, so the log defaults to <preview>/.land-work/verifier.log. On StepFailure it returns output_path=verifier_log and then calls cleanup_preview(), which removes the preview. All three verify failures in session 9f13ca23 (09-19 15:38, 09-20 23:49, 09-20 23:55) report output_path=/tmp/land-work-preview-XXXX/.land-work/verifier.log after 'cleanup: passed'. The agent then had to recreate a preview by hand (e53yb8el) and rerun task test-standard to see the failure.
findings.recommendation: Default land.py's verifier --log to a path outside the preview (e.g. $XDG_STATE_HOME/bento/land-work/<repo>/<branch>-<ts>.log) and include the log tail in the failure JSON. Add a test asserting output_path exists after a failed run.
findings.agent_root_cause: rdtn.4 and rdtn.14 were fixed and tested independently, and no test covers them together. The rdtn epic closed on code merge, while shatter memory project_land_work_verifier_first_run_flake ('just retry') is still the working procedure.

verify.note: run-verifier.py:351 defaults the log to <candidate>/.land-work/verifier.log. land.py:126 returns it as output_path, then cleanup_preview() runs at :367 before the JSON is emitted. Transcripts show output_path pointing at /tmp/land-work-preview-{g663hhnu,jus6t3ug,mz7t9g27}/.land-work/verifier.log. Correction to the recommendation: run-verifier already computes diagnostics.verifier_log_tail (run-verifier.py:138), but land.py drops it. Propagating that tail is the cheap half of the fix. Compounding factor: shatter's scripts/land_work_verifier.sh sends every gate to >/dev/null 2>&1, so even a preserved log would hold little (see bento-13).

dedupe.note: rdtn.4 (closed) made the verifier persist its raw log, by default at <candidate>/.land-work/verifier.log, which is inside the preview. rdtn.14 (closed) added land.py, whose finally block always removes the preview. Together they delete the log that land.py reports as output_path, so rdtn.4's goal is not met on the land.py path. Reopen rdtn.4 or file a follow-up that references both.

findings.title: Beads hooks add ~300s to every worktree/preview/merge; bento scripts hide it, the guard forbids the workaround, and its message cites a reference with nothing on hooks
findings.evidence: The shatter hooks are beads v0.63.3 with BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT default 300; installed bd is 1.1.0. land.py create_preview took 234.9-301.2s across 11 successful landings. Every launch-work-bootstrap --apply exceeded the Bash timeout (09-19 14:30 >120s; 09-21 22:09 >600s; this audit's own launch >120s). Background outputs contain "beads: hook 'post-checkout' timed out after 300s" 8 times, including this session's bevju0yf6. At least 4 sessions read .git/hooks/post-checkout trying to explain the hang. The guard blocked --no-verify on 09-21 15:55 and 09-22 16:20 with 'see the launch-work skill's dependency-bootstrap guidance for slow-hook fixes', but dependency-bootstrap.md contains only lockfile installers and ext4 disk notes.
findings.recommendation: Create throwaway preview worktrees with beads hydration suppressed for that subprocess (e.g. BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT=5 in the child env), with the reasoning documented. Time git subprocesses in bootstrap and create-preview, and warn with the hook name when one exceeds 30s. Add a doctor check comparing the beads hook marker version with bd version and measuring hook latency. Write the slow-hooks section the guard message cites.
findings.agent_root_cause: Bento treats beads as a first-class tracker but never budgets for its hooks. The guard was written against the symptom (bypassing) without fixing the cause, and nothing checks that the references a message cites exist. Shatter's fix (str-qwua7.28) has been open 18 days and contradicts str-mpgg1.

verify.note: The shatter post-checkout hook has marker 'BEADS INTEGRATION v0.63.3' with _bd_timeout=${BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT:-300}; bd version is 1.1.0. The guard message (require-worktree-git-guard.py:229-234) cites 'dependency-bootstrap guidance for slow-hook fixes', but dependency-bootstrap.md has zero matches for 'hook' or 'slow'. The transcripts contain 32 'hook post-checkout timed out after 300s' strings in total. create_preview durations were 234.9-301.0s, with one outlier of 10.9s. launch-work-bootstrap.py:302-310 runs git worktree add untimed. The finding is valid; the bento-side fix (doc section, timing warning, doctor version check) is distinct from shatter's str-qwua7.28.

dedupe.note: The shatter side is covered: str-qwua7.28 (open) installs BEADS_HOOK_TIMEOUT and retires the bypass guidance, and str-mpgg1 (in_progress) reverted the hook-env edits. The bento side is new: bento scripts do not suppress hydration for throwaway previews and do not time git subprocesses. The doctor has no hook-latency or hook-version check (rdtn.1 did not add one). The guard message added by rdtn.15 cites a reference with no hooks section.

findings.title: The git guard (rdtn.15) is bypassed by /usr/bin/git, rtk git, cd-to-primary, git -C and GIT_CONFIG env; a real bypass was observed
findings.evidence: Synthetic payloads (exit 2 = blocked): 'git merge feature' in primary exits 2, but 'git -C <primary> merge', 'cd <primary> && git merge', '/usr/bin/git merge', '/usr/bin/git commit --no-verify', 'rtk git commit --no-verify', GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.hooksPath env, 'git update-ref refs/heads/main', 'git switch main' all exit 0. Real bypass: session c1689435, 2026-09-22 00:48, '/usr/bin/git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push -u origin str-hjrnp.3'. Shatter memory recommends /usr/bin/git and the dotfiles RTK rule mandates an rtk prefix, so the forms left unchecked are the ones agents most often use.
findings.recommendation: Match (^|/)git and 'rtk git'. Resolve the effective repo from -C and from preceding cd in the segment chain. Add switch and update-ref on the primary ref, and check GIT_CONFIG_* env assignments. Add a table-driven test with these cases.
findings.agent_root_cause: The guard's tests use the bare 'git' form, and nobody checked it against the command forms the global and project guidance tell agents to use.

verify.note: _find_git_segments (guard :132-146) requires tokens[idx] == 'git' exactly, so '/usr/bin/git ...' and 'rtk git ...' are never inspected. _parse_git_invocation skips '-C <path>' without resolving the repo. The repo is taken from the payload cwd, so 'cd <primary> &&' is not considered. Env assignments are skipped, not inspected, and switch/update-ref are not handled. Real bypass confirmed: transcript c1689435 contains '/usr/bin/git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push -u origin str-hjrnp.3' (and .1). Additional: any command containing LAND_WORK_MARKER is exempted wholesale (:207). I did not rerun the synthetic payloads; this is a code read.

dedupe.note: rdtn.15 (closed at 2e05d33) claims to block branch-mutating git in the primary checkout. It matches only a bare 'git' token with cwd, so /usr/bin/git, rtk git, git -C, a preceding cd and GIT_CONFIG_* env all get past it, and a real bypass was observed. Its 30-case test table has none of these cases. Reopen it or file a follow-up linked to it.

findings.title: land.py aborts or hard-resets merge state in the shared primary checkout even when it did not start the merge
findings.evidence: abort_primary_merge_if_in_progress() runs 'git merge --abort' whenever <primary>/.git/MERGE_HEAD exists. It is called on every StepFailure, BaseException and SIGINT/SIGTERM, including failures at prepare, create_preview or verify, before the driver has touched the primary. The tree-mismatch path runs 'git reset --hard HEAD@{1}' in the shared primary. Shatter memories feedback_swarm_shared_checkout_landing_race and feedback_primary_checkout_diverged_local_main show concurrent sessions do use the primary. I did not observe a collision caused by this; it is a code-read risk.
findings.recommendation: Track self.merge_started and the pre-merge SHA. Only abort or reset when this driver started the merge, and reset to the recorded SHA rather than HEAD@{1}.
findings.agent_root_cause: Written assuming a single agent per primary checkout; no concurrent-session tests.

verify.note: land.py:144-148 aborts whenever <primary>/.git/MERGE_HEAD exists. It is called from every StepFailure/BaseException/signal path (:349, :368, :378), including prepare and verify failures before the driver touched the primary. :204 uses reset --hard HEAD@{1}. This is a code-read risk only, and no collision has been observed, so medium confidence is appropriate.

dedupe.note: No bento issue covers land.py aborting or resetting merge state it did not start in the shared primary checkout. Loosely related: bento-jwv (closed; an expedition failed merge leaves the worktree mid-conflict), which is a different script and the opposite failure.

findings.title: land.py runs 10-25 min with no invocation guidance; agents pipe it through tail and failures return exit 0
findings.evidence: The skill shows only 'land-work/scripts/land.py --runtime <runtime>'. Session 9f13ca23 ran 'land.py --runtime claude 2>&1 | tail -100' 14 times. Four failed runs ('prepare: failed', 'create_preview: failed', 'verify: failed') came back '[exited with code 0]'. Typical duration: create_preview ~300s + verify 266-578s + merge_push 259-1108s. Other sessions each invented their own '> log; echo exit=$?' plus background-polling pattern.
findings.recommendation: Add a canonical invocation block: run_in_background, stdout JSON to a file, stderr progress to a log, and check the exit code explicitly. Have land.py create its own progress log, print its path first, and emit a heartbeat every 60s.
findings.agent_root_cause: The skill documents what the driver does, not how an agent with a 2-minute foreground Bash limit should run it. The shatter memory lesson on piping through tail was never pushed upstream into bento.

verify.note: SKILL.md:258-262 shows only 'land-work/scripts/land.py --runtime <runtime>', with no guidance on backgrounding or exit codes. Transcript 9f13ca23 has 36 occurrences of 'land.py --runtime claude 2>&1 | tail -100', and failed runs show '[exited with code 0]'. land.py itself correctly returns 1 on failure (:385); the exit code 0 comes from the pipe to tail. Durations are confirmed (merge_push 258-1108s).

dedupe.note: No bento issue covers invocation guidance, a progress log or a heartbeat for the long-running land.py. On the shatter side, str-qwua7.26 (open) covers a related rule (the 2-minute foreground limit and no foreground sleep) but not land.py. rdtn.14 required one line per step but set no rule for background or piped runs.

findings.title: land.py forces rebase-before-land (--require-up-to-date) although the preview already verifies the exact merge
findings.evidence: Observed prepare failures: 'current branch is behind the primary branch by 2 commit(s)' (87606e10, 09-20 04:53), 'by 4 commit(s)' (9f13ca23, 09-21 15:19), and 'no commits ahead; behind by 1' (09-20 23:23). Each forced a rebase (post-checkout hook ~300s), a force-push (pre-push task affected) and inflated Stop-hook unpushed counts. create-preview merges the feature into the leased SHA and the verifier checks that exact tree.
findings.recommendation: Drop --require-up-to-date from land.py or make it advisory; a preview merge conflict should still produce a 'rebase needed' error. If a repo wants rebase-first as policy, make it a verifier.json or swarm-config option.
findings.agent_root_cause: Carried over from the manual flow (step 5 rebase) without rechecking it against the exact-candidate verification land.py already does.

verify.note: land.py:274 passes --require-up-to-date, and the preview does merge onto leased_sha, so the rebase is technically redundant for verification. However, rebase-first is documented deliberate policy: SKILL.md:239 step 5 says 'Rebase onto the preferred primary-branch base'. It was not an unexamined carryover. Making it configurable is reasonable, but this is a policy trade-off (linear, reviewable branches versus hook cost), and most of the cost is really bento-03's 300s hook. Lowered to P3.

dedupe.note: No issue questions land.py passing --require-up-to-date (rebase-before-land) when the preview already verifies the exact merge.

findings.title: Doctor seen/decided state lives in a per-checkout .agent-mode.local, so linked-worktree sessions get the full nudges every time
findings.evidence: Running the doctor in-process: in the audit worktree seen=frozenset(), so both full dormancy paragraphs and the superpowers notice ('prints once per repo') are emitted. In the primary seen={'bugshot','storystore'}, with one-liners. Shatter forbids work in the primary, so every working session gets the uncollapsed text, and the doctor writes a fresh .agent-mode.local into each worktree root. The guard's hook_bypass=allow opt-out has the same per-checkout scope.
findings.recommendation: Resolve .agent-mode.local through git rev-parse --git-common-dir (the primary checkout's copy) for reads and writes in the doctor and both require-worktree hooks.
findings.agent_root_cause: rdtn.2 was tested with the session cwd at the repo root. No test covers a session in a linked worktree, which is the only mode bento's own launch-work allows.

verify.note: The doctor resolves root via 'rev-parse --show-toplevel' (agent-env-doctor.py:198) and reads root/.agent-mode.local (:588, :775, :946), which is per worktree. The audit worktree has its own .agent-mode.local, created 2026-09-22 12:16, with the seen keys. The primary's copy also carries a 'dangerous' line that the worktree copy lacks, so the per-checkout split also drops the dotfiles launcher settings in worktrees. I did not independently rerun the doctor in-process.

dedupe.note: rdtn.2 (closed at e28b1c9) stored the doctor's seen/remind_after state in .agent-mode.local to collapse repeat nudges. The issue itself says that file is per-clone, and in practice it is per-checkout, so every linked-worktree session still gets the full nudge. rdtn.2's stated goal, collapsing repeats, is not met there. findings.title: Stale-preview doctor check spans all repos, prints one line per directory, and bento's test suite leaks ~90 previews into /tmp
findings.evidence: /tmp has 89 land-work-preview-* directories (86 created 09-22, 3 on 09-21). (now deleted) and holds fixture files (feature.txt, README.md, swarm-config.json), i.e. a test leak. default_preview_dir hard-codes dir='/tmp' (create-preview.py:84-85). check_stale_previews globs tmp_root with no repo scoping, emits one warning per entry and says 'let closure clean it up'. closure --apply choices are only the two branch-deletion modes (closure-scan.py:1659-1660).

findings.title: check-unpushed counts @{u}..HEAD, overcounting after rebases, and blocks on peer commits in the shared main
findings.evidence: Stop-hook blocks in shatter transcripts: 'str-6vl7p-redundant-canonicalize has 71 unpushed commits' (10x), '69' (10x), 'str-rmcrl... 72' (6x). Also "branch 'main' has 2 unpushed commits" (17x) and 'main has uncommitted changes and 1 unpushed commit' (13x) in the shared primary, where peer sessions leave commits.

findings.agent_root_cause: The hook assumes one session per checkout and linear branch history; no rebase or concurrency fixtures.

findings.title: Swarm skill has the lead land from inside the teammate's worktree, the practice a shatter lesson records as causing collisions
findings.evidence: swarm SKILL.md Serial-Mode Landing step 3: 'Invoke bento:land-work from within the teammate's worktree'. land.py needs the branch rebased there (see bento-07). Shatter memory feedback_lead_landing_prep_separate_worktree.md (2026-09-08): the lead's checkout and rebase in teammate worktrees 'silently moved the worktree's HEAD out from under them' while they were doing review fixes.
findings.recommendation: Have the lead land from a lead-owned scratch worktree at the teammate's branch tip, or require confirmation that the teammate session has exited. Add 'land.py --branch <name>' so it can run from any worktree.

findings.title: Agents busy-wait on background tasks with sleep-1/echo and ReadNotifications loops, burning hundreds of turns
findings.evidence: Since 09-04 there were 820 `sleep N[; echo x]` calls in 12 sessions and 600 ReadNotifications polls. Session 87606e10 (claude-sonnet-5, 09-19 to 09-21) made 1,575 tool calls, of which 609 were `sleep 1; echo ok` ('No-op wait for code review notification') and 598 were ReadNotifications. It produced 541 assistant turns starting 'Still waiting' and 934,138,123 cache-read tokens. Session 9f13ca23 made 201 `sleep 1` calls with description 'yield'. The agent writes 'I'll wait for the background task notification instead of polling.' and then keeps polling. The harness block text says 'Do not chain shorter sleeps to work around this block.' ScheduleWakeup was also misused 5× ("`prompt` is required when `stop` is not true"). There were 1,078 'Still waiting/Waiting' turns across all sessions. (scripts: aggregate.py, conventions.py cmd:sleep_busy)
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Waiting for background work' rule to dotfiles docs/agent-guidance.md. After launching a run_in_background task, end the turn, or use TaskOutput block=true, or one until-loop run in the background. Never use sleep<=5/echo loops or repeated ReadNotifications. Back it with a dotfiles PreToolUse hook that denies bare `sleep N` / `sleep N; echo X` commands and denies more than 3 consecutive ReadNotifications with no other tool call in between. Reword AGENTS.md 'Team-lead liveness … never idle' so it means event-driven checks, not continuous polling.
findings.agent_root_cause: No global instruction explains that ending the turn is how to wait. AGENTS.md says 'never idle', and the Stop hook blocks turn end during landings (see sessions-10), so the model invents a no-op loop that slips past the harness's sleep block. Nothing detects repetitive no-op tool calls.

verify.note: I recounted session 87606e10: 1575 tool calls, 609 bare `sleep N[;echo]` calls and 598 ReadNotifications. Session 9f13ca23 had 200 sleeps and 0 ReadNotifications. AGENTS.md:403-408 does say the lead must 'actively poll… never idle'. I'm lowering this to P2 because it wastes tokens and turns but produces no incorrect repository behaviour. The recommended PreToolUse deny-hook is reasonable. It should also cover the Stop-hook interaction from sessions-10.

The dotfiles tracker (GitHub issues, no beads) has nothing on it. bento-hkk (open, team-lead liveness monitoring) is loosely related.

findings.title: bento hook-bypass guard is evaded by /usr/bin/git, timeout/nice/env/rtk prefixes; used in the wild
findings.evidence: `_find_git_segments` only matches when `tokens[idx] == "git"`. I piped a PreToolUse payload into the installed guard. Exit 0 (allowed): `/usr/bin/git commit --no-verify -m x`, `/usr/bin/git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit -m x`, `timeout 60 git push --no-verify`, `rtk git commit --no-verify -m x`, `env git commit --no-verify`. Exit 2 (blocked): `git commit --no-verify -m x`, `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push`. In the wild, session c1689435 on 09-21T23:03 to 09-22T02:00 ran 13 commits/pushes of the form `/usr/bin/git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit -q …`. The guard shipped 09-10 (bento c9d7eaa/5210e74). shatter memory project_rtk_wrapper_corrupts_redirects steers agents to /usr/bin/git (256 uses since 09-04), and 4c6e73e3 used `timeout 60 git push --no-verify`.
findings.recommendation: In the guard, match `os.path.basename(tok) == 'git'`. Skip leading wrapper commands (timeout N, nice -n N, ionice, env [VAR=..], command, rtk, sudo) before looking for git. Also catch `GIT_CONFIG_*`/`-c core.hooksPath` spellings via GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS. Add table-driven regression tests for every spelling above.
findings.agent_root_cause: The guard was tested only against the canonical `git …` spelling. Repo memory independently tells agents to call /usr/bin/git, so the common real-world spelling was never exercised. There is no telemetry on successful bypass spellings.

verify.note: I piped payloads into the bento source guard. It allowed `/usr/bin/git commit --no-verify` (exit 0), `timeout 60 git push --no-verify` (exit 0) and `/usr/bin/git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit` (exit 0). It blocked bare `git commit --no-verify` (exit 2). _find_git_segments only matches when tokens[idx]=='git' (require-worktree-git-guard.py ~line 145). Session c1689435 contains 22 hooksPath-bypass commits and 18 pushes spelled `/usr/bin/git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null …`. P1 is justified: a policy-enforcing guard is trivially evaded, and that evasion is happening in practice.

findings.title: Pre-commit hook runs the full shatter-core test suite (incl. e2e) per commit — slow, fragile, and the main driver of bypasses
findings.evidence: precommit-rust.sh runs `cargo test "${pkg_args[@]}"`, which is all of shatter-core: 3,345 lib tests plus integration/e2e suites. It then runs clippy. Measured since 09-04: git commit with hooks median 60 s / p90 124 s versus 2 s with --no-verify. git push with hooks (pre-push `task affected`) median 80 s foreground / 308 s background, max 728 s. Failures unrelated to the diff: 9f13ca23 09-19T14:09 'TypeScript frontend not built: …/shatter-ts/dist/main.js does not exist' in a fresh worktree; 87606e10 09-19T15:58 discover_configs tests failing on ambient /tmp/.shatter; b6375e4e 'Go build timeout under sustained ~100-170 load average'. Each preceded a --no-verify. The landing verifier then reruns the gates on the merge preview (land.py median 780 s), so every change is gated three times.
findings.recommendation: Make pre-commit fast and hermetic: `cargo check`/`clippy -D warnings` on the staged crates only, target ≤30 s, no e2e. Keep tests in pre-push but have it accept a fresh verifier/affected receipt for the same tree (str-35vtk.24/.25). Wrap hook-invoked gates in run-heavy. Document the per-hook budget in CONTRIBUTING and AGENTS.md.
findings.agent_root_cause: Hook cost has no budget or measurement. str-npdt added the pre-commit test run without a latency target, and gate-dedup work (str-35vtk) never covered pre-commit. Agents learned to route around the hook instead of reporting its cost.

verify.note: scripts/precommit-rust.sh:33 runs `cargo test -p shatter-core/-p shatter-cli` (the full suite, integration tests included), then clippy. It also runs cargo test in shatter-rust and shatter-rust-runtime when those change. Neither the hooks nor precommit-rust.sh reference run-heavy (grep found nothing). I did not recompute the latency medians. The design flaw is clear from the code, and bypasses citing it appear in transcripts. P1 is borderline and P2 would also be defensible. I'm keeping P1 because this hook is the main driver of the bypass culture.

dedupe.note: str-35vtk.24 and .25 (open) cover the pre-push/verifier receipt half. str-jttrf (open) covers hook-run test fragility through GIT_DIR leaks. Nothing tracks making pre-commit fast and hermetic (no full shatter-core/e2e suite, a ≤30 s budget), hooks calling run-heavy, or a documented per-hook budget. str-npdt (closed) is where the heavy hooks came from.

findings.title: Concurrent sessions overload the host and collide on shared state; no load-aware scheduling for hooks/landing
findings.evidence: AskUserQuestion texts: 'System load just hit 141 (32 cores) from many concurrent sessions (kapow, pickpackit, other shatter previews)' (87606e10 09-19); 'System memory is critically tight (swap nearly full)' (9f13ca23 09-19); 'A concurrent session on this machine (Codex process(es) also active in this repo) appears to have deleted my in-progress land-work preview worktree mid-build' (9f13ca23 09-21). c1689435 measured load average 109→39. `uptime` during this audit: load average 173.86. Since 09-04 agents ran 49 `ps aux/-e`, 23 uptime/loadavg, 16 pgrep and 10 `free` calls in 15 sessions diagnosing load. The pre-push `task affected` and pre-commit `cargo test` do not go through run-heavy (grep of hooks: no run-heavy).
findings.recommendation: bento should provide one machine-wide admission control that land.py, the verifier and git hooks all use: run-heavy semaphore plus a load/memory check that waits instead of failing. Preview dirs should be owned by a lock so closure and other sessions cannot delete a live one. Shatter hooks should call gates via run-heavy. Add a 'machine busy' status line to land.py output so agents stop hand-diagnosing load.
findings.agent_root_cause: run-heavy is opt-in per command. Hooks and cross-project sessions (kapow, pickpackit, Codex) bypass it, and no component owns host-level capacity, so each agent rediscovers load and asks the user.

verify.note: Hooks and precommit-rust.sh do not use run-heavy (confirmed). I did not re-verify the load-quote transcripts or the count of diagnosis commands. The claim that a concurrent session deleted a preview is only the agent's own attribution, so it is unverified. The recommendation (machine-wide admission control plus a preview lock) is a large design item; treat it as a direction, not a scoped issue. Medium confidence.

dedupe.note: bento-dyp7 (open) is the host-wide weighted admission governor. bento-e583 (open) covers a preview worktree destroyed mid-verification by a concurrent session. str-35vtk.12/.13/.19 (open) are Shatter-local semaphores, leases and pressure-aware waiting. findings.title: bento check-unpushed Stop hook blocks every turn on conditions the agent does not own, forcing continuation during long landings
findings.evidence: There were 219 blocks across 44 sessions, 77 of them in 21 sessions since 09-04. 9f13ca23 had 31 blocks out of 95 stop events while land.py ran in the background, and the agent said 'Still mid-landing (land.py is running in the background) — that hook will clear once this branch merges'. 8 blocks since 09-04 were for the shared primary: "Session end blocked: branch 'main' has 2 unpushed commits" (87606e10, 9f13ca23, 5617a8ed). The hook message itself says 'Note: Stop fires at the end of every turn, not only when the session truly ends'.
findings.recommendation: Suppress the block when a background land.py/push task from this session is still running. Suppress it for branches or checkouts the session did not modify (the primary 'main'). Otherwise downgrade it to a once-per-session advisory. A true session-end check belongs in SessionEnd.
findings.agent_root_cause: A 'session end' invariant is enforced on a per-turn event. That removes the agent's legitimate way to wait (ending the turn), which feeds the busy-wait loops in sessions-01.

verify.note: check-unpushed.py:460-462 emits 'Session end blocked: branch … Stop fires at the end of every turn…', which confirms the per-turn blocking semantics. Line 39 shows some advisory throttling exists, so part of the recommendation (a once-per-session advisory) may already be implemented for some paths. I did not recount the block totals (219 and 77). The causal link to the busy-waiting in sessions-01 is plausible but inferred.

dedupe.note: bento-neng (in_progress) covers the per-turn re-nag and throttling. bento-k23u (closed) fixed blocking subagents under a lead hold. Not covered: suppressing the hook while this session's background land.py or push is running, suppressing it for checkouts the session did not modify, and moving the real check to SessionEnd. bento-2p2p (open, Beads path coupling) is related.

findings.title: Multi-issue feature epic built and landed before a cheap feasibility probe; the benchmark concluded the premise could not be measured

findings.title: Global hooks reference $DOTFILES, which is unset in many sessions: 94 hook failures and silently skipped session summaries

findings.title: bento git guard false-positives on quoted text / heredocs containing 'git merge'
findings.evidence: During this audit, a read-only `python3 - <<'EOF' … re.search(r'land\.py|land-work|task affected|task check|git merge|push origin', …)` run with cwd=primary checkout was blocked: "Blocked: 'git merge' mutates the checkout in the primary checkout". `_SEGMENT_SPLIT_RE = re.compile(r"&&|\|\||[;&|\n]")` splits inside quotes and heredoc bodies, so the ` git merge` fragment becomes a segment. The workaround was writing the probe to a file.
findings.recommendation: Split with a quote- and heredoc-aware tokenizer (e.g. bashlex, or shlex with punctuation_chars plus heredoc stripping). Add tests where 'git merge' appears inside quotes, heredocs and grep patterns.
findings.agent_root_cause: The guard was tested only on positive cases. No negative corpus of realistic agent commands (python heredocs, grep patterns) was used.

verify.note: I reproduced it. A python heredoc containing the regex string 'git merge', run with cwd set to the primary checkout, was blocked (exit 2, "Blocked: 'git merge' mutates the checkout"). _SEGMENT_SPLIT_RE splits on newlines and ; inside heredoc bodies and quotes.

dedupe.note: The false positives come from the git guard that bento-rdtn.15 added (closed). No existing issue covers quote- or heredoc-aware tokenizing. File as a new follow-up that references rdtn.15; it could be combined with sessions-02's guard rework.

findings.title: Shell text tools still dominate over Read/Grep/Glob; global rule conflicts with harness bypass-mode guidance
findings.evidence: Since 09-04: 655 Bash calls led by grep/cat/sed/find/head in 34 sessions (grep 372, cat 151, sed 70, find 58), versus Read 379, Grep 128, Glob 11. All-time: 1,470 versus 1,429. The worst session is 87606e10 with 111. `find` failures run at 10.3% (6/58), including an rtk rejection: 'rtk find does not support compound predicates or actions (e.g. -not, -exec)'. verify.note: The conflict is real. The bypass-permissions harness text explicitly permits cat/grep/sed via Bash, and the global AGENTS.md says to prefer Read/Grep/Glob. str-qwua7.26 is open at P2. findings.title: `task --list-all --json` in a meta test poisons Task checksums; CI `task check` has run no test suites since 2026-08-30
findings.evidence: test_every_emitted_gate_is_a_real_task runs subprocess ['task','--list-all','--json'] with cwd=ROOT inside meta (check-static). Scratch repro on go-task 3.50: a meta task running `task --list-all --json`, then `task: sub:test` with sources, prints 'Task "sub:test" is up to date' on a fresh tree and again after a source edit; with --dry, the test executes. Latest CI job log: task check took 78 s (16:53:47-16:55:05); rust-rt:test, go:vet, go:test, ts:test, cli:test, rust-fe:test, core:test-ignored, conformance and parity all 'is up to date'; the only 4 'test result:' lines come from the shatter-llm step. .task/ is gitignored and not cached. CI duration per day was 6-11 min before 2026-08-28 and 3-4 min every day since 2026-08-30. Local gate-times.csv: median successful check 286 s before (n=61) vs 59 s after (n=49).
findings.recommendation: Use `task --list-all --json --dry` or parse the YAML. Add a meta regression test asserting .task/checksum is unchanged by meta. In CI, use a fresh TASK_TEMP_DIR or check-fresh (str-qwua7.2). Make gate-wrapper report executed vs cached leaves and fail under CI=1 if any test leaf was cached. Run the real suite on main now. Close str-qwua7.3 with this root cause and report the mutating --json listing upstream to go-task.
findings.agent_root_cause: Gates are validated by exit code and workflow shape (test_ci_workflow_structure.py), never by proof that tests executed; two separately reviewed efficiency changes (str-35vtk.8, str-35vtk.21) combined into a hollow gate; cache semantics live only in private memory; str-qwua7.3 has sat uninvestigated as a P1 for 17 days.

verify.note: I reproduced the mechanism myself with go-task 3.50.0 in a scratch dir, using `includes: sub: {taskfile: ./sub, dir: ./sub}`. Running `task --list-all --json` on a fresh tree writes .task/checksum/sub-test. After that, `task sub:test` prints 'is up to date' and does not run, even after a source edit. Without the listing, the control run behaves normally (runs, then reruns after an edit). The meta test at scripts/test_affected_gates.py:203-212 does run that listing, was added 2026-08-29 (8ae14f13), and is wired into meta at Taskfile.yml:459. In today's CI log (run 35756993223), 11 tasks are cached: cli:test, conformance, core:test-ignored, docs-smoke, go:test, go:vet, parity, rust-fe:test, rust-rt:test, ts:install and ts:test. Only 4 'test result:' lines appear, all from the shatter-llm step. core:test-ignored, which carries all core unit and E2E tests, is cached, so core tests do not run in CI either. str-qwua7.3 and str-qwua7.2 are still OPEN as P1. I did not independently check the per-day CI duration numbers or the gate-times.csv medians.

dedupe.note: str-qwua7.3 (open) asks why tasks stay 'up to date' after the checksums are deleted. This finding gives the root cause: the meta test's `task --list-all --json` mutates the checksums. str-qwua7.2 (open) covers check-fresh and executed-vs-cached reporting. Neither issue records the new consequence that CI `task check` has run no suites since 2026-08-30. str-35vtk.21 was closed on the strength of a 'green' CI run, and that green is now suspect. bento-rdtn.6 (closed) added an executed flag to the verifier contract but does nothing for CI.
