findings.evidence: bento swarm/scripts/swarm-discover.py:18-21 reads only swarm-config.json (repo root, .claude/ or .codex/), and no such file exists, so swarms fall back to serial mode. The .md file's gates (/check-all, /pre-completion, /walkthrough-review) are at best read as prose. check-all has disable-model-invocation: true, so a swarm lead cannot invoke it through the Skill tool.
findings.recommendation: Write .claude/swarm-config.json with the landing block (mode, gate_scope: task affected, full_gate: task check) per bento references/landing-config.md, and delete the .md. Reference `task check` directly rather than /check-all.
findings.agent_root_cause: A plugin config format changed with no migration notice to consumer repos, and nothing validates repo swarm config.

verify.note: Confirmed. Only .claude/swarm-config.md exists. bento 2.3.82 swarm-discover.py reads only swarm-config.json (repo root, .claude/ or .codex/). check-all has disable-model-invocation: true at line 5. I did not verify that swarms fall back to serial mode.

dedupe.note: str-35vtk.9 (open) assumes 'bento:swarm reads swarm-config.md' and plans to rewrite the .md, which is now stale because bento-96ua.2 (closed) moved to swarm-config.json with a landing schema. str-qwua7.54 notes the .codex/swarm-config.md symlink. No issue covers migrating to .claude/swarm-config.json. File as new and update the str-35vtk.9 scope.

findings.title: Instrumentor data-flow map ignores program point; recorded path constraints contradict the concrete execution
findings.evidence: There is one end-of-function dataFlowMap (instrumentor.ts:187), and it is used for every branch (instrumentor.ts:1710). Assigning an unresolvable value does not drop the old binding (instrumentor.ts:498). Loop bodies are visited once. Probes: stale() `let x=a; if(x>0)...; x=b` records branch 0 as `b > 0`. staleUnknown() `x=opaque()` records `a > 10`. loopCarried() records `(0+1) < 3` and `a+1 > 10` (actual a+3). Real frontend execute of stale with inputs [5,0] returns branch_path taken=true, constraint {gt, param b, 0}, which is false for b=0. A bd full-text search found no existing issue.
findings.recommendation: Snapshot the flow map at each branch while instrumenting. Mark a variable unknown when it is reassigned from an unresolvable expression. Treat variables assigned inside a loop as unknown at the loop head. Add an oracle test: evaluate each recorded branch_path constraint on the concrete inputs and assert it equals `taken`. Add a core-side consistency check using triage::evaluate_constraint that downgrades inconsistent constraints to unknown and records them in telemetry.
findings.agent_root_cause: The only documented parity contract (shatter-ts/CLAUDE.md:10-19, root CLAUDE.md 'Parallel parity') is about which AST node types are handled, not about semantic correctness. Property tests compare builders in isolation with a fixed resolver. No gate checks that a constraint evaluated on the concrete inputs matches `taken`.

verify.note: Checked instrumentor.ts:187: a single buildDataFlowMap is built at finalize. Line 1710 uses ctx.dataFlowMap for every branch. Line 498 skips the set when the new value is unknown, so the stale binding stays. Reproduced with dist/instrumentFunction on stale(a,b) {let x=a; if(x>0){x=b;...} x=b}: it emits __shatter_branch(0,1,!!(x>0),{gt, param b, 0}), which is wrong. Did not re-run the loop or opaque probes. P1 is justified because the recorded constraints can be false for the concrete path.

dedupe.note: No open issue covers flow-map facts that are wrong for a given program point, or constraints that contradict `taken`. Closed str-4kop (SSA phi/ite for conditional reassignment) and str-mu3h (closures over mutable state become unknown) address neighbouring precision problems but not this soundness bug. File as new; reference them and fold the implementation into the shared walker (frontend-ts-09 / str-rf2v).

findings.title: switch/ternary/value-position &&,|| analyzed but never instrumented; analyze vs instrument branch IDs desync and core misattributes coverage
findings.evidence: Probe mixed(): analyze gives [[0,16,ternary],[1,17,if]], while instrument emits __shatter_branch(0, 17, ...). sw() and tern() get branchCount=0 from the instrumentor. For logic() (const ok = a>0 && b>0), analyze reports logical_and but instrument emits 0 branch calls. extract_targets_inner joins analysis.branches[].id with runtime discovery ids, so a run that takes the `if` marks the ternary covered and reports the `if` as Uncovered. Closed issues str-w0d.1 and str-sunh claim switch/ternary constraint emission. CLAUDE.md:286 mentions the switch gap only in passing.
findings.recommendation: Use one branch enumerator shared by the analyzer and the instrumentor, or return the instrument id->line map and join on (line, type) in the core. Instrument switch cases (eq(discriminant, case) per case), ternaries and value-position logical expressions. Add an alignment test over a fixture corpus asserting analyze (id, line) == instrument (id, line).
findings.agent_root_cause: Issues were closed on unit evidence without a known-answer e2e test for each branch type. The limitation was written into CLAUDE.md prose and an e2e workaround (reading raw_results) instead of being filed. No invariant checks analyze/instrument ID alignment.

verify.note: Reproduced mixed(a): analyze returns branch 0 as the ternary on line 2 and branch 1 as the if, while instrument emits __shatter_branch(0, 2, a>5), so the two ID spaces diverge. instrumentor.ts:1393-1411 only adds __shatter_record for switch cases, and the instrumentor has no isConditionalExpression handling. coverage_metrics.rs extract_targets_inner joins analysis branch.id against discovery ids, so the misattribution follows. The str-w0d.1 description does list 'if, switch, ternary, &&, ||', and it is closed. str-sunh is only tangentially related (React ternary in JSX). CLAUDE.md:285-287 has the raw_results workaround note.

dedupe.note: Closed str-wsg added switch/ternary/logical branch extraction to the TS analyzer only. The instrumentor was never extended, so analyze and instrument IDs desync. No open issue covers instrument-side coverage or ID alignment; str-qwua7.35 is the Go-only builder unification. File new and cite str-wsg as the incomplete predecessor.

findings.evidence: Probe shadow(xs, x) with xs.filter((x) => { if (x > 5) ... }): the analyze condition is {param x} > 5, so the inner x is treated as the outer param. Builders resolve by name only (paramNames.has(expr.text)). Only the analyze output was observed.

findings.title: Target errors mentioning 'timeout' are classified as outcome timed_out / category infrastructure
findings.evidence: Real-frontend probe: a target that throws RangeError('timeout must be positive') for ms<=0 returns outcome {status:'timed_out', short_reason:'timeout must be positive'} and thrown_error.error_category='infrastructure'.
findings.recommendation: Only harness-owned timeouts should produce timed_out: ERR_SCRIPT_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT, plus a dedicated error class thrown by the async Promise.race at executor.ts:1276. Target errors should be classified by type, not by message substring.
findings.agent_root_cause: There are no negative tests for the classification heuristics. Message-substring classification is not flagged by any review checklist.

verify.note: executor.ts:281-286: classifyError returns 'infrastructure' for any message matching /timed?\s*out/i, and 'timeout must be positive' matches. TIMEOUT_PATTERNS at 331-338 also includes the bare 'timeout'. isTimeoutError at 3293 maps infrastructure plus a timeout-classified message to timed_out. The code path supports the claim; I did not re-run the live probe.

dedupe.note: No issue about classifying outcomes by the 'timeout' message substring. Related outcome work (str-hy9b.A5, str-jeen.41, str-o7b8z) is closed and different. Analogous Rust-side pattern: str-qwua7.33 (classify by downcast, not substring).

findings.title: Async timeout race leaks an uncleared 15s timer per async execution; jest forceExit hides leaked handles
findings.evidence: Promise.race([syncResult, new Promise((_, reject) => setTimeout(reject, timeoutMs))]) never calls clearTimeout. jest.config.js sets forceExit: true ('avoid hanging on worker threads').
findings.recommendation: Call clearTimeout in finally (or unref the timer). Drop forceExit and run once with --detectOpenHandles to find and fix the real leaks.
findings.agent_root_cause: forceExit was added to silence hangs instead of finding their root cause, which removed the signal that would have exposed this leak.

verify.note: executor.ts:1274-1281 calls Promise.race with a setTimeout that is never cleared or unref'd, and jest.config.js sets forceExit: true. Each leaked timer lasts at most timeoutMs and holds no big resources, and the frontend is a long-lived process, so the practical impact is minor. Downgraded to P3; dropping forceExit is still a sound recommendation.

dedupe.note: No issue mentions forceExit, clearTimeout, detectOpenHandles or leaked timers in shatter-ts.

findings.title: parseRequest validates only the envelope; missing fields crash as internal_error; validCommands hand-maintained
findings.evidence: Real-frontend probes: {command:'execute'} with no fields returns internal_error 'Unhandled error: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes')'. {command:'analyze'} returns file_not_found 'File not found: undefined'. parseRequest returns `parsed as Request` after checking only id, protocol_version and command. validCommands duplicates the generated ALL_COMMANDS. The ts-conventions skill requires validating incoming data and parsing it into typed discriminated unions.
findings.recommendation: Add per-command field validators that return invalid_request naming the bad field, preferably generated from registry.yaml field_model. Derive the dispatch set from ALL_COMMANDS.
findings.agent_root_cause: The ts-conventions rule is not backed by any test or lint. The conformance cases only send well-formed requests.

verify.note: handlers.ts:1113-1159 checks only id, protocol_version and command before `return { request: parsed as Request }`. The validCommands literal at :1151 is hand-maintained. I did not re-run the internal_error probe, but the code makes it plausible. Note that ts-conventions says 'Prefer', not 'must'.

dedupe.note: No issue on per-command field validation in parseRequest or on deriving validCommands from ALL_COMMANDS. str-4btb (closed) only consolidated the parseRequest tests. Related: str-qwua7.7 (registry extractors pointed at real sources).

findings.title: Preflight requires node_modules whenever project_root is set; dependency-free projects fail and one failure blocks every later request
findings.evidence: Probe: analyze with project_root set to a directory without node_modules returns preflight_failed 'missing_node_modules', even for a file with no imports. project_root comes from the nearest package.json/tsconfig.json/go.mod/Cargo.toml, so a tsconfig-only package or a .ts file in a Go repo qualifies. preflightFailure is one module-level value, so it applies to every root. Not verified end to end through the shatter CLI.
findings.recommendation: Require node_modules only when package.json declares dependencies or devDependencies, or fail lazily on MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Key the failure per root.
findings.agent_root_cause: There is no fixture for a zero-dependency TS project; the walkthrough and e2e examples all live in dependency-installed trees.

verify.note: handlers.ts:190-218 requires node_modules whenever project_root is non-empty. project.rs MARKERS includes tsconfig.json, so a tsconfig-only project fails. The stickiness across roots is intentional: the code comment and CLAUDE.md say 'one failure authoritative'. It is a design choice to revisit, not a bug. End-to-end CLI impact was not verified (per the finding too), and whether the core passes a Go/Cargo root to the TS frontend is unverified. Downgraded to P3.

dedupe.note: str-jeen.26 (closed) introduced the TS node_modules preflight, and str-jeen.40 (closed) made it preflight_failed. Neither handles dependency-free projects or scopes the failure per root, so the introduced behavior is a regression. File new and cite both.

findings.title: Common operators and nodes collapse to unknown (??, **, shifts, element access, conditional, as/!, template literals)

findings.agent_root_cause: P3 items from the prior audit's area report were not filed.

verify.note: Reproduced: `const v = a ?? 7; if (v>3)` records {unknown} > 3, and `xs[i] === 7` records {unknown} eq 7. I did not probe ** or `!`. P3 is appropriate.

findings.title: Branch-type capability claims closed without per-type known-answer e2e tests; test workarounds recorded in prose instead of filed
findings.evidence: str-w0d.1 and str-sunh (closed) claim switch/ternary/logical constraint emission, but frontend-ts-02 shows it does not exist. The enum-domain e2e reads raw_results specifically because switch emits no branch_path, and that is documented as a note rather than filed. The root CLAUDE.md models integration tests on known-answer functions, but there is no TS fixture for each BranchType.
findings.recommendation: Add a TS known-answer fixture for each BranchType (if, else_if, switch, ternary, logical_and, logical_or, while, for, do). It should assert analyze/instrument ID alignment and that both outcomes are discovered via branch_path. Add a parity or drift-patrol check that every analyzer-emitted BranchType is also instrumented, per frontend. Add 'workarounds in tests must be filed as issues' to the completion checklist.
findings.agent_root_cause: The completion checklist accepts unit tests plus an e2e run on if-heavy examples. No gate enumerates branch types, and agents write limitations into CLAUDE.md instead of filing them in bd.

findings.title: Crate-bridge harness shares stdout with user code; any function that prints fails as internal_error
findings.evidence: The crate-bridge driver writes its result with println!(serde_json::to_string(&exec_result)) and redirects no file descriptors. The standalone and dispatch harnesses do redirect with dup2 (executor.rs:2524-2561). PersistentHarness::execute treats the first stdout line as the response. Probe: crate with `pub fn noisy(n:i64)->i64{println!("hello from user code {n}"); n+1}`, executed with harness_mode crate_bridge, returned `error internal_error output parse error: failed to parse execute result: expected value at line 1 column 1 line: hello from user code 1` and outcome runtime_failed. Sibling calls after the harness restarted worked (quiet(5)=10). Crate-bridge is the automatic fallback whenever bin_only returns NonExecutable for a file inside a crate.
findings.recommendation: Give the protocol its own channel in the crate-bridge driver. Either dup the original stdout to a private fd at startup and dup2 /dev/null or a capture file over fd 1 around each call (no libc dependency needed: std::os::fd plus a small unsafe block, or reopen /dev/stdout), or prefix protocol lines with a sentinel and skip non-sentinel lines in the reader. Add a regression test with a printing function in crate_bridge mode. Update the CLAUDE.md side-effect contract and the parity matrix.
findings.agent_root_cause: The parity contract only records that crate-bridge does not capture console output, which framed the issue as missing capture rather than a protocol corruption risk. No conformance or E2E fixture contains a printing function in a crate-bridge-routed crate.

verify.note: executor.rs:5195 crate-bridge driver emits the result with println! and has no dup2. dup2 appears only in the standalone and dispatch generators (executor.rs:2541-2561, 2720-2881). The parity-matrix note (around line 491) says fd redirection happens only in the standalone and dispatch harnesses. I did not re-run the probe; the code path matches the claim.

dedupe.note: No issue covers crate-bridge harness stdout sharing with user prints. Closed crate-bridge issues str-qsrb and str-70m2 deal with target bloat and cache invalidation, not the protocol channel.

findings.title: Hand-rolled runtime constraint JSON is invalid for float `1.` and control-char strings, and silently degrades to unknown
findings.evidence: constraint_for_lit uses f.base10_digits(), so `x > 1.` becomes `"value":1.`. escape_json_string escapes only backslash, quote, \n, \r and \t, so U+0001 is embedded raw. Instrumenting a probe file gave `branch_hit(0u32,2u32,...,"{...\"value\":1.}}")`. The explore artifact lists both constraints as kind unknown, with the raw JSON as the hint. runtime branch_hit falls back to SymConstraint::Unknown with no warning. In concolic explore, `if s == "a\u{1}b" {return 2}` was never reached in 60 iterations. The analyzer's typed builder emits 1.0 and "a\u0001b" correctly for the same source.
findings.recommendation: Fold into str-qwua7.36 as a correctness bug, not only an operator gap: build protocol::SymExpr and serialize it with serde_json. Until then, emit a stderr warning or a counter from branch_hit when parsing fails, and add a proptest that every instrumented constraint string parses as JSON.
findings.agent_root_cause: str-qwua7.36 was scoped as a coverage and parity gap, so nobody tested encoder validity. The runtime's silent Unknown fallback hides the failure from every gate. There is no invariant test that instrumented constraint JSON parses.

verify.note: instrument.rs:671-712: floats emit f.base10_digits() raw, and escape_json_string handles only backslash, quote, \n, \r and \t, so other control chars are not escaped. runtime lib.rs:180-186 falls back to SymConstraint::Unknown silently. str-qwua7.36 is open and folding this into it is sound. I did not re-run the explore probe.

dedupe.note: str-qwua7.36 (open) replaces hand-formatted JSON with serde SymExpr and calls the encoder 'a second place to get escaping/shape wrong'. It does not name the concrete invalid-JSON cases (float `1.`, control chars) or the silent fallback to unknown. Add these as a correctness bug plus the parse-warning and proptest acceptance items.

findings.title: Match-arm constraints encoded as string equality on pattern source text; analyzer mis-encodes binding+guard arms
findings.evidence: For `match n {0=>..,1..=5=>..,k if k>100=>..,_=>..}` with n:i64, the runtime emits `{param n} == {const str "0"}`, `"1 ..= 5"`, `"k"` and `"_"`, and the param node has no path field. The analyzer's static condition for the `k if k > 100` arm is `n == "k"` (str). In concolic explore of `clean` (n+1>5, then this match), all 60 iterations used n=0: only returns 4, 1 and 2 were reached, never 3, 5, 6 or 7. The markdown said 3 paths while the batch line said '6 paths, 5/7 branches'. CLAUDE.md:83 describes the core compensating with alphanumeric matching of raw token text.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the analyzer's typed pattern-to-SymExpr conversion (int literal: eq; range: and(ge,le); binding: true, or the guard's expression; wildcard: negation of the earlier arms, or omit) in instrument.rs. Fix the analyzer's binding+guard arm. Add an E2E known-answer fixture with an int match that needs Z3, with no minable literals, and retire the core's token-text workaround afterwards.
findings.agent_root_cause: The E2E known-answer fixtures use enum or literal matches that literal mining can solve, so string-typed arm constraints never failed a gate. The core-side workaround (str-mambd) treated the symptom instead of pushing back on the frontend encoding.

verify.note: instrument.rs:418-446 builds eq(param <match expr tokens>, const str <pattern tokens>) for every arm, including bindings and wildcards, and the param node has no path field. I did not independently verify the analyzer's binding+guard mis-encoding or the explore run counts.

dedupe.note: str-qwua7.36 would share the analyzer's SymExpr builder with instrument.rs, but its scope lists only let patterns, arithmetic, bitwise and calls. Match-arm string-equality encoding, the analyzer's binding+guard mis-encoding, and the core token-text workaround are not tracked. File as new, linked to qwua7.36.

findings.title: Inverted timeout budget: request timeout (30s) is no longer than the build timeout, so cold Rust builds surface as a generic request timeout
findings.evidence: CLI --request-timeout defaults to 30s. The CLI-governed SHATTER_BUILD_TIMEOUT is 30s. The frontend fallback DEFAULT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECS is 120 (eeceb7b4), while PARITY.md:96 still says 30s. The first execute does cargo build and run inside one request. Under load, explore on two trivial functions gave `concolic observe failed: frontend error: request timed out after 30s` with 0 iterations at 32.7s. A rerun with --request-timeout 180 --build-timeout 170 succeeded.
findings.recommendation: Guarantee request_timeout > build_timeout + exec_timeout for requests that may build: derive it, or give prepare/first-execute its own budget. Have Rust build progress or cold-build state produce a specific diagnostic that names --build-timeout/--request-timeout. Fix PARITY.md:96.
findings.agent_root_cause: Timeout defaults are governed per env var (the cli_parity_tests constants) but there is no invariant across them. The PARITY table was not updated when eeceb7b4 changed the fallback.

verify.note: args.rs:562 has request_timeout default 30, and PARITY.md:84 gives the CLI build-timeout default as 30s. executor.rs:1017 DEFAULT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECS=120, but PARITY.md:96 still says the Rust fallback is 30 s. Linked to str-qe9pp. I did not re-run the timed-out explore.

dedupe.note: str-qe9pp (open) records that conformance rust/prepare_supported_rust times out at the 30s request timeout, but not the root cause (request timeout <= build timeout). findings.title: str-qwua7.50 (poison-tolerant locks) targets an unreachable failure; the real gap is no panic boundary in the handler
findings.evidence: Handler::run and dispatch have no catch_unwind, so any panic ends the process (main exits with 1) and a poisoned lock can never be seen by a later request. qwua7.50's acceptance test ('a request that panics while holding the lock, followed by a normal request on the same handler, succeeds') therefore cannot pass as written. The cache Mutexes are only accessed from the dispatch thread. The spawned threads (executor.rs:3055, 3206, 5475) only forward child stdout.
findings.recommendation: Re-scope qwua7.50: wrap dispatch in catch_unwind and turn panics into an internal_error response (clearing caches), then add poison recovery; or replace the Mutexes with plain owned maps, since access is single-threaded. Keep the module-docs half as is.
findings.agent_root_cause: The audit-filed issue was written from a pattern heuristic (lock().unwrap() in a long-lived process) without checking whether the process catches panics. Issue-readiness review does not require verifying the failure scenario.

verify.note: There is no catch_unwind in handler.rs or main.rs. The only catch_unwind calls are in generators.rs native invoke and in generated harness code. main exits on a handler error, and a panic aborts the process. Correction: the qwua7.50 acceptance test is not impossible, because a unit test can wrap the handler call in catch_unwind itself and then reuse the handler. What cannot happen is poison recovery in production, since a panic kills the process before a later request arrives. The recommendation to re-scope around a dispatch panic boundary is sound.

dedupe.note: str-qwua7.50 (open) prescribes poison-tolerant locks. The finding re-scopes it: add a catch_unwind panic boundary in dispatch, or drop the Mutexes. Update qwua7.50 rather than filing a new issue.

findings.title: 38 Rust-FE tests silently pass when cargo cannot reach the network

findings.title: shatter-rust-runtime harness loop swallows malformed requests; thread-local tracking drops user-thread branches
findings.evidence: `serde_json::from_str(line).unwrap_or_default()` turns a malformed request into Null, so the handler runs with empty inputs and reports a misleading 'input 0 deserialization failed'. The flush_results fallback interpolates the error text into JSON without escaping. STATE is thread_local, so branches executed on std::thread or rayon threads spawned by user code are silently lost; the Rust CLAUDE.md does not mention this (only the tokio flavor is handled).
findings.recommendation: Return an explicit protocol-error result for unparseable requests. Build the fallback JSON with serde_json::json!. Document the thread-local limitation in CLAUDE.md and the parity matrix, or switch to a process-global recorder behind a Mutex keyed by execution id.
findings.agent_root_cause: The runtime crate has no CLAUDE.md or contract doc, and its tests cover only the happy-path API.

verify.note: runtime lib.rs:558/612 use serde_json::from_str(line).unwrap_or_default(), and STATE is thread_local! at :167. I did not inspect the flush_results escaping claim.

dedupe.note: Closed str-dfnu2 and str-oc67 fixed thread-local coverage loss for tokio cross-worker awaits by switching harnesses to a current-thread runtime. findings.title: shatter-llm parser/rate-limit gaps: int width ignored, first-bracket-only extraction, uncapped backoff, no PBT
findings.evidence: type_matches uses `TypeInfo::Int { .. } => v.is_i64() || v.is_u64()`, ignoring int_width and int_signed, so -1 passes for u8. extract_first_json_array tries only the first '['. The backoff `Duration::from_millis(100u64 << attempt)` has no cap: shift overflow panics in debug at attempt 64, and at 20 retries it sleeps about 29 hours. Retry-After is not capped. parse.rs has 10 example tests and no proptest, although it parses untrusted model output.
findings.recommendation: Validate integer range against width and signedness. Scan successive '[' candidates until one parses. Cap the backoff (for example min(2^n*100ms, 30s)) and cap Retry-After. Add a proptest that parse_response never panics and only returns type-conforming vectors.

findings.title: Z3 translation splits one numeric param into unrelated Int and Real variables; solver returns wrong SAT models
findings.evidence: `to_z3_expr` prefers the per-comparison hint sort whenever it is Int/Real-compatible with the declared sort (:500-503). `to_z3_real`/`to_z3_int` pass Real/Int hints. `VarTable` keeps separate ints and reals maps under the same name, and `extract_concrete_values` inserts ints then reals into one HashMap (the Real overwrites). Direct call of `solve_for_new_path` with x:Float, constraints [x>0.5 (float const), NOT(x<1 (int const))], negate idx 1 → `Ok(Sat({"x": Float(1.5)}))` in 3/3 runs, although 0.5<x<1 was wanted. With n:u8, [n<1000.5, n>300.5] negate 1 → `Sat({"n": Float(0.0)})`: the u8 range bound binds only the Int twin. End to end: `shatter explore mix.go --concolic --max-iterations 40 --clean` → Classify 23 iters, 2 paths, worklist_exhausted, 4/5 lines. `return "low"` is never reached; the tried inputs contain no value in (0.5,1). The Go frontend emits `{op:gt, const float 0.5}` and `{op:lt, const int 1}`. The random/hybrid engine (which also has the Z3Solver strategy) misses it at 100 iterations too.
findings.recommendation: Choose one Z3 sort per variable from `param_sorts` before translation and coerce at use sites (`Real::from_int` / `to_int`) instead of declaring a second const. Assert in `extract_concrete_values` that no name appears in two sort tables. Add a solver unit test and a Go/TS E2E known-answer fixture shaped like Classify (nested x>0.5 / x<1 on a float param).
findings.agent_root_cause: The solver proptests (str-r6fr) never generate one param under mixed sorts, and E2E known-answer fixtures use only int or string params. The prior audit graded the solver 'good engineering' without a behavioural probe. There is no requirement that a concolic E2E fixture cover every numeric-type combination.

verify.note: Code confirms the mechanism. to_z3_expr (solver.rs:500-503) uses the hint sort whenever it is Int/Real-compatible with the declared sort. VarTable keeps separate ints/reals maps and calls Int::new_const(name) and Real::new_const(name) under the same name, which gives two distinct Z3 consts. extract_concrete_values inserts ints and then reals into one HashMap, so the Real overwrites the Int. assert_int_param_ranges binds only the Int twin. I re-ran the reviewer's mix.go fixture. `explore --concolic --max-iterations 40 --clean` gives Classify '23 iters, 2 paths', 80% (4/5 lines), so `return "low"` is never reached. Random mode also reaches only 4/5. I did not re-run the direct solve_for_new_path probe. No existing open issue covers mixed-sort params.

dedupe.note: No issue covers Int/Real sort split for one numeric param. Related: str-6ayh (closed) fixed string params being declared as Int by picking the sort from ParamInfo, which is the same class of bug. str-r6fr (closed) added solver proptests, but none catch this.

findings.title: --setup silently ignored in concolic mode: every production caller passes setup_context=None

The explore (pipeline_orchestrator), scan (explore_with_scan_mode) and observe concolic callers all pass `None` for `setup_context`, and the CLI gives no warning. str-0s76.6 was closed with 'orchestrator::explore() now accepts and threads setup_context … matching explorer behavior'. findings.agent_root_cause: The issue was closed on API-level test evidence without checking production callers. The E2E suites call mid-level APIs instead of the pipeline, despite the CLAUDE.md warning about modules 'silently disconnected from the pipeline'.

findings.title: str-qwua7.49 premise wrong: pool expect sites unreachable; real failure is empty pool → every queued task misreported as task timeout
findings.evidence: The sites use `sender.send(fe).await.expect`, not try_send. `checkout()` recv cannot return None because WorkerPool holds its own sender (shutdown drops it explicitly). `replace_dead_worker_if_needed` → `reap_dead_slot` on spawn failure can drive live_count to 0. `pool.checkout().await` inside each task then blocks until join_with_dynamic_watchdog fires, and the task is reported as a phase_timeout('task').
findings.recommendation: Detect live_count==0 with pending>0 and fail fast with ScanError::WorkerPoolExhausted{last_spawn_error}. Retitle and rescope str-qwua7.49. Add a regression test where every respawn fails.
findings.agent_root_cause: The prior audit filed the issue from a static read without checking channel ownership. Issue drafts are not cross-checked against code before filing.

verify.note: The str-qwua7.49 premise is wrong. There is no try_send in the file: :2240-2254 use send().await.expect on a max_workers-capacity channel. recv() cannot yield None because WorkerPool owns a sender. The hang path is narrower than stated. replace_dead_worker_if_needed calls reap_dead_slot on spawn failure, then maybe_grow(remaining) (:4743) immediately retries a detached spawn. live_count reaches 0 with blocked checkouts only when spawns keep failing. I did not verify that each task is then reported as phase_timeout('task'). The retitle/rescope recommendation is sound.

dedupe.note: str-qwua7.49 (open) targets the recv/try_send expect sites. The finding shows those sites are unreachable and that the real failure is an empty pool reported as task timeouts. Rescope and retitle str-qwua7.49 rather than filing a new issue.

findings.title: Invariant inference over-generalises: no minimum support at function level, constant confidence=1.0, only 0-anchored templates

findings.title: Z3 has no default query timeout; blocking solver can outlive timeout_explore
findings.evidence: The --solver-timeout help says 'Default: no limit', and set_timeout_msec is applied only when Some. With solver_offload the Z3 call runs on a blocking thread that deadline checks cannot cancel. The prior audit claimed 'Timeouts: cfg.set_timeout_msec on each query'.
findings.recommendation: Set a default per-query timeout (e.g. 2s, configurable) and record Unknown/timeout as a frontier stall.
findings.agent_root_cause: The audit accepted a code-presence claim without checking defaults.

verify.note: args.rs:658/1073 read 'Default: no limit', and solver.rs:1215 sets the timeout only if Some. Exception: helpers.rs:893 defaults it to 10s under --mcdc. The prior audit's 'set_timeout_msec on each query' is accurate only when a value is set. Stronger than claimed: main.rs:593 destructures the Scan command with `solver_timeout: _`, so `shatter scan --solver-timeout` is accepted and silently discarded, and scan always passes None.

dedupe.note: str-36cd (closed) added an optional solver_timeout_ms and a --solver-timeout flag, but set no default. str-w0d.3 (deferred) covers complexity-aware timeout allocation. No issue covers a default timeout, Unknown counted as a frontier stall, or the solver outliving timeout_explore.

findings.title: str-qwua7.37 rests on a wrong premise; implementing it as written would regress Go string solving
findings.evidence: The issue says Go's receiver:null call form 'cannot be solved' and mandates bare-name plus receiver. But string-ops.yaml declares `{language: go, method: "strings.HasPrefix", style: free}`, solver.rs receiver_and_first_arg has a 'Go-style: no receiver, two positional args' branch with tests, and live Go output for strings.HasPrefix(s,"go_") is {name:"strings.HasPrefix", args:[param s, const]}, which is solvable. The real divergence is method calls on values: live Go output for u.IsAdmin() is {name:"u.IsAdmin", args:[]}, so the receiver is dropped and collect_param_names loses param u. The issue also cites a wrong path (data/string-ops.yaml).
findings.recommendation: Amend str-qwua7.37. The canonical form keeps package-qualified free functions as name="pkg.Fn", receiver=null (per string-ops.yaml style: free). Method calls on values must emit name=bare and receiver=expr. Add a regression test that Go strings.* constraints stay solvable, and fix the file path.
findings.agent_root_cause: The audit-to-issue pipeline ran a 'confirmed during drafting' step that inspected only the receiver path of convert_string_call, and cross-check did not catch it. Issue text written as authoritative Step 0 can steer an implementer into a regression.

verify.note: The mechanics are confirmed. string-ops.yaml lists go 'strings.HasPrefix' style: free. solver.rs:919 has a Go-style no-receiver branch. callSymExpr (analyzer.go:2359-2385) emits name=exprString(Fun) with no receiver, so a value method call drops the receiver param, and collect_param_names (sym_expr.rs:138) walks only the receiver and args. The 'would regress' framing is overstated. The issue's premise is about method calls ('recv.Method'), and its acceptance criterion already allows 'receiver = expr or null', so a careful implementer would not break free functions. The ambiguity is real: the Step 0 claim that the receiver:null form 'cannot be solved' is wrong for package functions. The wrong path (data/ vs shatter-core/data/) is confirmed. Worth amending the issue text; P3.

dedupe.note: This amends open str-qwua7.37. Its Step 0 asserts that Go's name="recv.Method", receiver=null form is unsolvable and must become bare name + receiver. The finding says package-qualified free functions (strings.X) must keep pkg.Fn with a null receiver. Update str-qwua7.37's body; do not file a new issue.

The runtime branch_path constraint for c=='x' is also const str "x". `shatter explore` default explorer, 60 iterations: 3 paths, 6/7 lines, return 3 never reached. --concolic, 200 iterations (stopped at 24): 2 paths, 5/7 lines, missed both return 1 and return 3. verify.note: The locations are swapped in the evidence. protocol/analyzer.go:2345-2348 is the one using strings.Trim(lit.Value, "`\"'") for STRING and CHAR together. instrument/symextract.go:141-152 already uses strconv.Unquote for STRING correctly. findings.title: shatter-go-tool: non-atomic extract caches partial binary as executable; no HTTP timeouts; GitHub API call on every run; tests cover only arg parsing
findings.evidence: extractBinary opens targetBinary with mode 0755 and copies into it directly. With SHATTER_BUILD unset, latestContinuousBuild calls api.github.com before the cache check on every invocation (unauthenticated limit 60/h). downloadFile ignores GITHUB_TOKEN. main_test.go is 39 lines and tests only parseArgs.

Cache the resolved latest tag with a TTL and fall back to the newest cached build when offline. Add httptest-backed tests for manifest selection, checksum mismatch and partial-extract recovery.

findings.title: Explore report under-reports paths (0 or 1 shown) while 3 paths/classes were found
findings.evidence: The TS function fmt2 has 3 paths (n>10 'big', n<0 'neg', else throw). Three runs of `explore --clean --max-iterations 30` printed `[batch 1/1] fmt2: 30 iters, 3 paths, 2/2 branches` each time. The reports showed '**1 path(s)**' with only the throw row, then '**1 path(s)**' with only 'big', then '**0 path(s)** · **100%** coverage (5/5 lines)'. In that last run the spec in the same stdout said 'Behavioral classes: 3' (artifact-samples/edge-plain-spec.md). The artifact has observation.unique_paths=1 and one new_path_executions entry, while raw_results holds all three branch paths. classifyNumber is not affected. Root cause not isolated.
findings.recommendation: Derive the report's path count and rows from the same equivalence classes the spec uses. Add an E2E assertion that report path count == spec class count for the known-answer examples, and add this fall-through-throw fixture.
findings.agent_root_cause: E2E tests check branch coverage and solver results, not that the user-facing report agrees with the engine's own counts. The [batch] line and the report compute paths in different places (parallel-path problem).

verify.note: Reproduced with the fmt2 source (n>10 big, n<0 neg, else throw). Two `explore --clean --max-iterations 30` runs both logged `[batch 1/1] fmt2: 30 iters, 3 paths, 2/2 branches`. The reports showed `**0 path(s)**` in one run and `**1 path(s)**` with only the 'big' row in the other. The output changes from run to run, and a user can be told 0 paths while the spec shows 3 classes. I did not isolate the root cause and did not check explorer.rs:467. It may be that the report counts only 'new' paths beyond the seeds. That is still misleading output, so P1 stands, although P2 would be defensible because the coverage figures are correct.

dedupe.note: str-9q1z (closed) fixed report.rs conflating branch_count with unique_paths in the explore report. This finding is a different under-count: paths shown against classes found. str-qwua7.57 (open) unifies the behavior-class terminology. File as new.

findings.title: Mixed-language scan: second language sub-scan deletes the first's function artifacts and overwrites summary.json; checkpoint lives in a different dir
findings.evidence: `scan mix` (3 TS + 2 Go files) logged Go artifacts functions/00001..00004_...go__*.json, then TS artifacts 00001..00008 in the same scan-results/<64hex>/functions dir. Afterwards only the 8 TS files exist, and summary.json says total_functions 8, failed 0. The report says 12 discovered and 4 failed (artifact-samples/scan-summary.json vs scan-mix.json). The checkpoint default_path uses scan_id[..16] under project_root/shatter-artifacts and ignores SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR. Function artifacts use the full 64-hex id via HarnessStorage.
findings.recommendation: Give per-language sub-scans their own namespace, or merge them into one summary with global indexes. Run stale-artifact cleanup once per scan. Resolve the checkpoint path through HarnessStorage and the same scan root. Add a two-language scan test asserting every reported function has an artifact and a summary entry.
findings.agent_root_cause: Scan tests are single-language. The artifact layout is undocumented (SPEC §6.2 describes only the checkpoint), so no reviewer had a contract to check against.

verify.note: scan-mix.err shows all 12 artifact writes going to the same scan-results/896e5a62... dir. The Go sub-scan used indexes 00001-00004 and the TS sub-scan reused 00001-00008. prepare_fresh_scan_artifact_root (scan_orchestrator.rs:593-609, called at 3912 after compute_scan_id at 3889) does remove_dir_all on functions/ in each per-language pass (str-14en grouping, scan.rs:1270). scan-summary.json has total_functions 8 and failed 0, while the report shows 12 discovered and 4 failed. Checkpoint::default_path (checkpoint.rs:197-203) hardcodes project_root/shatter-artifacts and scan_id[..16], ignoring HarnessStorage/SHATTER_ARTIFACT_DIR. Correction: the cited lines 552-565 are the scan_root helpers; the deletion is at 593-609.

dedupe.note: No issue covers a second language's sub-scan deleting the first's artifacts or overwriting summary.json, or the checkpoint living in a different directory. Related closed issues: str-9f6f (stale-artifact cleanup, the probable cause), str-4oa1 (per-language progress resets) and str-14en (mixed scan). Related open: str-8q1b4 (resume report parity).

findings.title: Spec markdown invariants render blank subjects, duplicate lines and '[1]' confidence
findings.evidence:
`explore --invariants --spec ts/01-arithmetic.ts:classifyNumber` prints '**Function invariants:**
-  != null [1] (100/100)
-  != null [1] (100/100)
-  is non-empty [1] (100/100)' (artifact-samples/ts-spec-invariants.md). format_path joins an empty path for scalar params/returns, and the markdown uses invariant.description (with no input/output target) plus the f64 confidence. The JSON already has good labels ('input.age is non-null') and YAML renders 'input is non-null', so only markdown is broken. The unit tests use synthetic 'x > 0' descriptions.
findings.recommendation: Render ClassifiedInvariant.label in markdown. Drop '[1] (n/n)' together with str-qwua7.61. Add a golden test of --invariants --spec output for a scalar function. Also suppress invariants that restate the precondition (input == 0) and trivial non-null lines.
findings.agent_root_cause: Spec rendering tests build synthetic invariants instead of running the detector on a real function. There is no golden output for --invariants.

verify.note: spec.rs:568-576 and 615-627 render `ci.invariant.description` with `[{confidence}] (sat/total)`. format_path is path.join('.'), so an empty path gives an empty subject. ClassifiedInvariant.label exists (invariants.rs:638) but markdown does not use it. The sample shows `-  != null [1] (100/100)` twice. The defect is real, but it only appears in the opt-in --invariants markdown and the JSON/YAML output is correct. That makes it a quality defect rather than broken core behaviour, so I lowered it to P2. It overlaps str-qwua7.61 for the confidence part.

dedupe.note: str-qwua7.61 (open) removes the '[1] (n/n)' confidence rendering. Blank subjects (label not rendered), duplicate lines, restated-precondition and trivial non-null invariants, and the golden test are not tracked.

findings.title: spec-diff misses a real behavior change and mispairs classes by branch id (false negative, not only noise)
findings.evidence: v1 grade: <0 invalid, <50 fail, else pass. v2 inserts n>100 -> 'overflow'. v1 'fail' and v2 'overflow' share BranchPath [(0,F),(1,T)] and get paired. spec-diff output (artifact-samples/sd-diff.txt): 'Summary: 2 added, 1 removed, 1 precondition(s) changed, 1 class(es) with insufficient comparison evidence', with [ADDED] 'fail', [ADDED] 'pass', [REMOVED] 'pass', [PRECOND] 'fail', [INCONCLUSIVE] 'fail'. 'overflow' is never reported, so the one real change (inputs >100 now return overflow instead of pass) is missing. Exit 1 only because of noise.
findings.recommendation: Match classes by behavior (postcondition plus symbolic path condition), not branch ids. Report CHANGED with both labels when a path's postcondition differs. Add this v1/v2 pair as a spec-diff known-answer test. Raise str-qwua7.38 to P1.
findings.agent_root_cause: spec-diff tests build SpecClass values by hand with stable ids. No test generates v1/v2 specs from real code with an inserted branch.

verify.note: The facts hold. sd-v1/v2 show v1 'fail' at [(0,F),(1,T)] and v2 'overflow' on the same path. The diff output never mentions 'overflow', and the paired class is reported only as INCONCLUSIVE plus a PRECOND change. The root cause, pairing by exact BranchPath, is already filed as str-qwua7.38 (P2, open), with the same file:line and recommendation. The new part is that renumbering can hide a real change (a false negative), not only add noise. File this as evidence on str-qwua7.38, not as a new finding. The tool still exits non-zero here, so I would not raise it to P1 on this example alone. Leave the priority bump to the maintainer.

dedupe.note: str-qwua7.38 (open, P2) covers pairing classes by behavior instead of BranchPath, but frames the problem as noise (spurious added/removed). The false negative (a real postcondition change missed) and the v1/v2 known-answer test are new evidence. Add them to qwua7.38 and raise it to P1.

findings.title: The gauntlet scan-failure check has matched nothing since 2026-05-13; its tests pin the dead format; allowlist and CLAUDE.md reference removed fixtures
findings.evidence: SCAN_ERROR_SUMMARY_RE matches 'N error(s)'. Commit 00124c84 (2026-05-13, str-izhn) changed the summary to 'Scan complete: **1 completed**, **4 failed**, ...'. Running the checker on today's scan stdout, which has 4 failed and 7 interrupted functions, exits 0 with no output. Failed functions do not appear as '| FAIL |' rows and print no [error]/[warn] lines (grep count 0 in scan-mix.err). The tests still use 'Scan complete: **1 function(s)** tested, **0 skipped**, **0 error(s)**'. The allowlist's expected_scan_errors names 11-opaque-types.ts and 12-external-deps.ts, which are not in the examples checkout. The str-jeen.57 fix (closed 2026-05-08) was dead five days later. There are four divergent copies of the step checker, and the Docker gauntlet has no FAIL/summary check.
findings.recommendation: Have gates consume scan's JSON (codebase.failed_functions, failed[]) or a single machine-readable summary line. Generate checker fixtures by running the CLI rather than hand-writing strings. Use one shared checker for all four demo scripts. Fold into str-qwua7.10 and update CLAUDE.md and the allowlist.
findings.agent_root_cause: The checker and the CLI output have no shared contract, and the checker's tests validate it only against strings its author wrote. Changing a user-facing format triggered no check for downstream parsers.

verify.note: SCAN_ERROR_SUMMARY_RE (gauntlet_check_output.py:30-32) needs 'N error(s)'. Production scan code never emits 'error(s)' (checked with /usr/bin/grep). The summary is now 'Scan complete: {} completed, {} failed, ...' (scan_orchestrator.rs:6120, from commit 00124c84 on 2026-05-13). FAIL_ROW_RE is also dead: report.rs:2302-2315 (str-4ad5) emits only PASS/WARN/LOW, and a test at report.rs:4886 asserts that no '| FAIL |' row appears. So every expected_failures entry with outcome: FAIL in the allowlist is dead as well, which the finding does not mention. Running the checker on scan-mix.stdout (4 failed, 7 interrupted) exits 0. test_gauntlet_check_output.py:31 still pins the old format. 11-opaque-types.ts and 12-external-deps.ts are missing from the standalone/ts examples checkout (they exist only under typescript/src in an old /tmp checkout). This overlaps str-qwua7.10 but adds the concrete reason the check is dead.

dedupe.note: str-jeen.57 (closed) claims the gauntlet fails on scan FAIL/error rows, and str-jeen.59 (closed) added the allowlist. The finding shows the checker has matched nothing since 2026-05-13 because the format changed. str-qwua7.10 (open) covers demo gates' bad sanity checks but not the dead scan-format regex, the tests pinning the dead format, or the stale allowlist and CLAUDE.md fixtures. Fold into qwua7.10 or reopen jeen.57.

findings.title: Spec preconditions are sample statistics (often wrong or vacuous); symbolic path constraints already in the artifact are not used
findings.evidence: fmt2's 'big' class (n>10) has precondition 'param[0] > 0', which is false (n=5 throws). The throw class has 'typeof param[0] == "number"'. All three categorizeUser classes have 'SameType object' (ts-spec-invariants.json). classifyNumber 'zero' has 'param[0] == 0' from 33 identical samples. Each raw_results branch_path carries constraints such as {op:gt,left:{param n},right:{const 10}}. The 2026-09-04 audit's recommendation 11 was never filed as its own issue.
findings.recommendation: Emit the path condition (conjunction of branch constraints, rendered as source-like text) as the precondition. Show sample statistics separately as 'observed inputs'. Suppress preconditions shared by every class.
findings.agent_root_cause: The audit-to-issue pipeline merged this recommendation into a spec-diff issue and it was dropped. No test checks precondition correctness on a known-answer function.

verify.note: edge-plain-spec.md shows the 'big' class (n>10) with precondition 'param[0] > 0', and the throw class with 'typeof param[0] == "number"'. The same pattern appears in sd-v2 ('fail' gets SameType number). I did not check whether audit-2026-09-04 recommendation 11 was ever filed. No open issue for this turned up in quick searches.

dedupe.note: str-0oc (closed) specified 'preconditions for each class derived from constraints'. The finding shows preconditions are sample statistics and the path constraints go unused. str-dcz (closed) promised a precondition-change diff. The 2026-09-04 audit item was never filed. No open issue.

findings.title: Three incompatible spec JSON shapes; compare rejects the --spec-out bundle, the only clean producer
findings.evidence: `compare ts-spec-out.json go-spec.json` gives 'Error: failed to parse spec A ...: missing field `function_name` at line 172', exit 2 (compare-ts-go.txt). With the bare FunctionSpec extracted by hand it works: '4 of 4 shared behaviors match' (compare-ts-go-bare.txt). The bare form only exists on --spec-json stdout, which is polluted by markdown. `properties` emits a YAML list of bundles. spec-diff on TS vs Go bundles reports 'Added functions: ClassifyNumber / Removed functions: classifyNumber' without pointing to compare.
findings.recommendation: Use one spec reader for all consumers that accepts bundle, bare spec, and bundle list. Add `compare --function A[=B]` for multi-function bundles. When names differ only by case or language, have spec-diff suggest compare.
findings.agent_root_cause: Each consumer command owns its own deserializer. No cross-command round-trip test runs 'produce with explore, consume with compare'.

verify.note: compare.rs:19-21 deserializes both inputs directly as FunctionSpec. The --spec-out file is a versioned bundle ({version,file,functions:[...]}). compare-ts-go.txt shows 'missing field `function_name`', and the hand-extracted bare spec works. A bd search for 'compare' found no duplicate; str-dfcb7 and str-lsvnm are unrelated.

dedupe.note: str-wfqh (closed) made spec-diff accept FileSpecBundle, but compare still rejects the --spec-out bundle. str-nq20 (closed) added cross-language compare. str-qwua7.11 (open) covers the stdout mix. No issue asks for a single shared spec reader or `compare --function`. File as new.

findings.title: No published schema for spec, scan report, explore artifact, summary/manifest/run-status; SPEC §5 and PROJECT-LAYOUT describe outputs that do not match reality
findings.evidence: protocol/schemas has 22 protocol schemas and none for outputs. SPEC §5.1 shows 'Explored: classifyNumber / Iterations: 50 / New paths: [1] ...', but actual output is a markdown table (ts-explore.md). §5.3 shows a bare spec, while --spec-out writes a versioned bundle. §5.6 claims scan JSON has behavior maps and analysis, but the real keys are discovered_inputs, behavior_clusters, constraint_stats and completion_outcome. §6.2 documents only scan-results/<16hex>/checkpoint.json, while runs write scan-results/<64hex>/{manifest,summary,run-status}.json, run-status.tsv and functions/. PROJECT-LAYOUT names recorded-mocks/ as 'the most clearly documented current artifact path' and omits explore-results/ and scan-results/. The plugin's interpret-shatter-spec skill expects shatter-artifacts/<name>.spec.json, which Shatter never writes.
findings.recommendation: Generate JSON Schemas from the serde types (schemars) into protocol/schemas/artifacts. Add a drift check to task parity or docs-smoke. Rewrite SPEC §5.1, §5.6 and §6.2 and PROJECT-LAYOUT from real output. Point plugin skills at the schemas.
findings.agent_root_cause: docs-smoke executes config and snapshot examples but not report examples. The schema discipline in protocol/GOVERNANCE.md covers only frontend messages, not user-facing artifacts.

verify.note: protocol/schemas contains 22 protocol *.schema.json files plus test_schema_validation.py and no output/artifact schemas. SPEC.md:792-805 shows the old 'Explored:/Iterations:/New paths' text format. §5.6 claims 'per-function behavior maps'. §6.2 documents only checkpoint.json with a 16-hex prefix. PROJECT-LAYOUT.md:249-252 says recorded-mocks/ is 'the most clearly documented current artifact path'. The shatter-agents interpret-shatter-spec SKILL.md:27 cites shatter-artifacts/<name>.spec.json. str-2fjn (protocol schema cross-validation) is adjacent but covers only protocol messages.

dedupe.note: No issue covers published JSON Schemas for output artifacts (spec, scan report, summary, manifest). str-ndb.4 covers only the frontend protocol schema. str-qwua7.9 (open) validates doc examples against structs. str-qwua7.21.1 (open) is the config reference. str-wurp (open) is the CLI-surface drift gate. All are adjacent; none covers SPEC §5 and PROJECT-LAYOUT being rewritten from real output.

findings.title: Spec YAML uses serde custom tags (!AllEqual) and is rejected by standard YAML loaders

findings.title: Scan report: 100% headline with 1 of 12 functions completed, absolute paths everywhere, two differing summaries, zero-row sections
findings.evidence: scan-mix.md: 12 discovered, 1 completed, 4 failed, 7 not attempted, but 'Overall coverage (completed-functions subset): 100.0%'. The HTML tile says just 'Coverage 100%'. Absolute temp paths appear in every table, in JSON file_path and qualified_id, and in artifact names (00001_tmp_claude-1000_-home-ketan-...__classifyNumber.json). With -o, stdout's '# Scan Results' table uses /abs::fn while the file uses Function|File columns. 'Interesting Inputs' lists 2 of 4 inputs with no stated rule. findings.recommendation: Lead with 'N of M functions completed' and show coverage over all discovered functions. Use project-relative paths everywhere, with project_root stored once in JSON. Use one summary shape on stdout and in files. Omit zero rows and empty sections. Define or drop 'Interesting Inputs'.
findings.agent_root_cause: There is no visual/golden review gate for scan reports. bugshot CLI capture is still pending (str-qwua7.53), and walkthrough-review is manual.

verify.note: The HTML part holds. scan_report.html:13-17 shows tiles 'Functions 1' (completed only), 'Paths Found 3', and an unqualified 'Coverage' bar at 100%, with no discovered or failed count. findings.title: Minor output defects: --format text keeps markdown, stray '# Shatter Explore' on stdout with -o, --spec dropped with --spec-out, analyze-only output thin, non-executable lines shown uncovered, Rust lang 'any', green 'complete with errors'

findings.title: Agent system: no producer/consumer contract or golden-output suite for artifacts
findings.evidence: Findings artifacts-02/03/05/06/07/09/13 are each a format drift between an output producer and a consumer: the gauntlet checker, compare, SPEC §5, plugin skills, or HTML-vs-markdown numbers. None of these consumers is tested against real CLI output. Issues str-jeen.57 and sa-tyb were closed on text-only changes without running the consumer.

findings.title: Conformance harness reuses a frontend after a timeout, so one slow reply cascades into misattributed failures
findings.evidence: The drift-patrol run at load average 66/103/116 reported 'FAIL go / execute_outcome_shape_go -- no response' plus 3 more timeouts, then 'go / shutdown -- id: expected 99, got 20'. Re-runs: `conformance_harness.py -f go` -> All checks passed (2.3 s), full harness -> 42 checks passed. `send()` returns None after a 30 s select and the loop `continue`s on the same process, so the late response to case N is read as case N+1's reply.
findings.recommendation: In `send()`, loop reading lines until one arrives whose `id` equals the request id (discarding stale ones). On a timeout, kill and respawn the frontend (re-handshake) before the next case. Report one 'timeout under load' failure instead of a cascade. Consider scaling COMMAND_TIMEOUT_S by a load-aware factor, as run-heavy does.
findings.agent_root_cause: The harness was only ever exercised on an idle machine. Gate-pressure policy (str-35vtk.19, open) does not cover the patrol. The prior audit's patrol run SKIPped conformance, so this path was never observed.

verify.note: conformance_harness.py:88-107: send() writes the request, waits once with select(timeout), then reads a single line. There is no id matching. On None, the loop at :609-615 records the failure and `continue`s on the same process, so a late reply is read as the next case's response. The logic is confirmed from code. I did not reproduce the cascade myself; the load average is currently about 92, so it is plausible.

dedupe.note: str-qe9pp (open) describes the Rust prepare timeout that causes an 'off-by-one id cascade'. str-uoclg (closed with the bare reason 'Closed') describes the same cascade 'masking the real root'. Both target the Rust symptom. Neither asks the conformance harness to match response ids, discard stale replies, or respawn after a timeout.

findings.title: `revalidate` does not detect output regressions: it ignores return values and counts path changes under code change as confirmed
findings.evidence: goals-runs/regress2: explored classifyNumber, then changed `return "zero"` to "nil" and swapped even/odd. `shatter revalidate 01-arithmetic.ts` printed '[drift] classifyNumber (expected drift)' twice, then '4/4 behaviors confirmed.', and exited 0. The JSON shows verdict 'confirmed' for input [0], whose return value changed from zero to nil. classify_verdict compares only branch path and error severity. SPEC §2.7 says revalidate compares 'observed against cached behavior. Exit 0 = no regressions'.
findings.recommendation: Include the return value and thrown error (with nondeterminism masking) in the verdict. Treat an output change on a replayed input as a regression regardless of fingerprint. Stop counting ExpectedDrift as confirmed for the exit code, or add --fail-on-drift and make it the default in CI mode. Add an E2E known-answer test that mutates a return value and requires exit 1.
findings.agent_root_cause: Unit tests only exercise the verdict matrix on synthetic severity and path inputs. No gate performs a real mutate-then-revalidate check. SPEC wording was not checked against behavior.

verify.note: Reproduced independently. I explored 01-arithmetic.ts, changed `return "zero"` to `return "nil"` and ran `shatter revalidate`. Every behavior printed '[ok] ... (confirmed)', the summary was '6/6 behaviors confirmed.', and it exited 0. classify_verdict (revalidation.rs:86-118) takes only code_changed, path_matches and severity, never the return value, and a path mismatch with code_changed maps to ExpectedDrift. This contradicts SPEC.md:459-462 ('Exit 0 = no regressions'). spec-diff on the same change does report [CHANGED] zero->nil, so the two regression paths disagree.

dedupe.note: str-kab3 (closed) specified comparing observed behavior against recorded behavior with a nondeterminism mask. str-3lob (closed) specified a nonzero exit on PotentialRegression. The finding shows that return values are ignored and path changes under code change count as confirmed, so the closed revalidation epic str-76z6 does not detect output regressions. No open issue.

findings.title: Explore silently resumes prior results across explorer modes and engine versions; --concolic reused random-explorer results and labelled them concolic
findings.evidence: goals-runs/ts-all-concolic.err: '[info] Found prior explore summary for 01-arithmetic.ts ... [resumed] classifyNumber ... Make explore resume opt-in (like scan --resume) or document it in SPEC §2.1 with a prominent '[resumed N/M]' summary line. Make --no-cache imply --clean, or document that it does not.
findings.agent_root_cause: Resume semantics differ between the parallel paths (scan: opt-in --resume; explore: implicit). This was found downstream and recorded only in agent memory, never filed or documented, so every engine-comparison experiment can be silently wrong.

verify.note: Reproduced. After a default explore of 02-strings.ts, `explore 02-strings.ts --concolic --no-cache` printed 'Found prior explore summary ... [resumed] classifyString ... (prior run)' for both functions, and the markdown labels each '*Explorer: concolic (Z3-backed)*'. SPEC mentions resume only for `scan --resume` (§6.3, line 251), never for explore. The defect is therefore the resume key and labelling, plus the missing documentation, not the existence of resume. The recommendation should keep auto-resume for interrupted runs but key it on explorer mode, budgets and engine.

findings.title: Line-coverage metric is inconsistent across languages: Go scan inflates to 100%, Rust deflates to ~50%
findings.evidence: Go: zolem scan (goals-runs/zolem-fixture-default.json) reports (*Loader).Load at branches 7/18 but lines_covered 15 / total_lines 15 (100%). The function spans loader.go:87-153; the executed lines are 88,89,93-95,99-101,104,108-110,138,145,152, so the loop body (111-136) and every error return never ran. The same pattern appears for (*fixturesYAMLSelector).Select (2/10 branches, 5/5 lines) and (*SequenceCounters).Step (2/6, 9/9). reconcile_line_coverage uses `instrumentable.unwrap_or(span).max(covered)`, which hides an undersized denominator. Rust: classify_number finds all four outcomes (3/3 branches) but reports 54% (7/13 lines), because shatter-rust sends no instrumentable_line_count; the parity matrix marks this not_supported and no open issue tracks it.
findings.recommendation: (1) Find out why the Go scan-path instrumentable count is at or below the covered count, and make the reconcile step warn or flag when covered >= instrumentable while branches are uncovered, instead of silently clamping. (2) Implement instrumentable_line_count in shatter-rust, and file an issue for it. (3) Add a cross-language known-answer E2E test: the same function in TS, Go and Rust with full branch coverage must report 100% lines, and a half-covered one must report under 100%. (4) Re-baseline the downstream goals only after this is fixed.
findings.agent_root_cause: The downstream 90% goals were defined on this metric without any test that it is correct. The parity matrix records the Rust gap as a known divergence, which stops it from being treated as a defect.

verify.note: Go: in the reviewer's zolem-fixture-default.json, (*Loader).Load shows branches 7/18 with lines 15/15, while zolem internal/fixture/loader.go has Load at 87-153 with the next func at 155, so a denominator of 15 is impossible. Select (2/10 branches, 5/5 lines) and Step (2/6, 9/9) follow the same pattern. (*wasmSelector).Select even reports lines_covered 3 against total_lines 0. observe.rs:143-145 does `unwrap_or(span).max(covered)`, which hides the undersized denominator. Rust: every constructor in shatter-rust/src/protocol.rs sets instrumentable_line_count: None, and parity-matrix.yaml:872-874 marks rust not_supported. str-szcn3 (Go instrumentable count) is closed, so the Go inflation is a new defect in that fix or the scan path, not a missing feature. I did not re-run the zolem scan and relied on the reviewer's artifact.

dedupe.note: str-szcn3 (closed) added Go instrumentable_line_count, but Go scan now inflates to 100%. str-uabz (closed) added the silent clamp in reconcile_line_coverage that hides it; the recommendation is to warn instead. str-hbky (closed) fixed the TS denominator, and no Rust equivalent exists: nothing tracks instrumentable_line_count for shatter-rust. There is no cross-language known-answer coverage test.

findings.title: Canonical examples are weakly explored and the failures are allowlisted rather than tracked; the TS analyzer widens discriminated-union literals to str
findings.evidence: Default explore of all 52 standalone TS functions at 100 iterations: 445/799 lines = 55.7%. The known-answer check against the EXPECTED BRANCHES comments in files 01-05 finds 24/39 expected outcomes. computeArea: 0/6 branches with both explorers; the analysis shows the `kind` field typed {"kind":"str"} in all three variants, and the generator emits {"kind":"true","radius":2.0}. The gauntlet allowlist has 17 permanent FAIL entries with no issue IDs, unchanged since 8734407f (2026-05-08). The walkthrough exercises only files 01, 02, 03, 04 and 18.
findings.recommendation: Turn the EXPECTED BRANCHES comments into a machine-readable known-answer manifest and add a gate that fails when found-outcome counts regress (a ratchet, not an absolute 100%). Link each allowlist entry to a tracker issue and fail the gauntlet when coverage for an allowlisted function drops below its recorded value. Fix TS literal-type preservation for object fields (emit enum_values / const literal for discriminants).
findings.agent_root_cause: Gates are tuned to stay green. The allowlist suppresses known effectiveness gaps with no owner and no ratchet, and the demo uses only the easiest examples.

verify.note: gauntlet-scan-allowlist.yaml is 113 lines with only 1 'str-' reference. It was last touched in 8734407f/398e4a7e on 2026-05-08, and entries like computeArea and routeRequest cite 'union-input synthesis' with no issue linked. In the reviewer's concolic run, computeArea reached 21 iters, 1 path, 0/6 branches. The artifacts show generated `kind` values such as "", "0", " " and random strings, never circle, rectangle or triangle, which fits the claim that literals are widened to str. I did not re-verify the 24/39 known-answer tally or the walkthrough file list. Minor: the allowlist header says it scans `examples/standalone/ts/`, but examples/ in the worktree contains only go/ and rust/, which needs its own check.

dedupe.note: str-qwua7.10 (open) makes the demo gates fail on 0% coverage and all-throwing functions, but it has no known-answer ratchet and does not link allowlist entries to tracker issues. str-knf0v (closed) emits enum_values for TS enums and literal-union aliases, but not for discriminant literals on object fields; that gap is new. str-v0yjq (open) covers honoring enum_values in the other core paths.

findings.title: The concolic (Z3) explorer does not outperform the default explorer on the project's own hard examples
findings.evidence: goals-runs/ts-sub-concolic (fresh directory, 21 functions from 9 files): concolic 164/454 lines (36.1%) against default 185/454 (40.7%). Concolic stops after 21-35 iterations on most functions (computeArea 21 iters, 0/6 branches; matchRoute 21 iters, 1/19; negotiateLanguage 23 iters, 1/12). classifyHttpResponse drops from 13/13 to 10/13 branches; validateEmail rises from 6/19 to 13/19. Kapow memory, 2026-07-02: '--concolic ... ZERO coverage delta vs random'. str-ior1 ('re-baseline Zolem with --concolic') was closed with the reason 'Closed' and no data.
findings.recommendation: Add a benchmark comparing default and concolic on the examples corpus (fresh artifacts, fixed seeds) and publish the delta per release. Investigate the early termination (worklist exhaustion or plateau before the budget) and the missing symbolic constraints on object-field discriminants. Until concolic wins measurably, stop describing the product as concolic-first in README and SPEC, or make the default scheduler's solver strategy the documented primary path.
findings.agent_root_cause: No effectiveness metric compares explorers, and closing str-ior1 without data hid the question.

verify.note: I confirmed the early termination from ts-sub-concolic.err: computeArea 21 iters, matchRoute 21 iters 1/19, negotiateLanguage 23 iters 1/12, classifyStatus 21 iters 0/3, and the summary is 164/454 = 36%. I could not independently confirm the default-explorer baseline of 185/454 for the same 21 functions, because no matching default-subset artifact exists in goals-runs. Line totals from markdown are also suspect given goals-03. str-ior1 is closed with the reason 'Closed'. The headline 'concolic does not outperform default' needs a controlled fresh A/B run before it is stated as fact; the premature worklist termination is the solid part.

dedupe.note: str-ior1 (closed) found the baseline was measured under the random explorer and asked for a re-baseline with --concolic. No issue benchmarks concolic against default on the examples corpus, investigates concolic's early termination, or questions the 'concolic-first' positioning.

findings.title: Downstream ≥90% coverage goals (kapow, zolem, pickpackit) have stalled at 18-28% since 2026-07-07 with no tracker ownership
findings.evidence: Last baselines: kapow 18.3% (07-01; resolver dir 18.8% on 07-06), zolem 28.0% lines (07-05), pickpackit 26.3% combined (07-07). findings.title: Spec preconditions remain single-sample equalities; spec-diff reports a semantic swap as precondition change plus inconclusive

findings.evidence: goals-runs/collide: a.ts:classify (returns a-big/a-small) and b.ts:classify (b-neg/b-pos) explored together produce a single .shatter-cache/behavior-maps/classify.json whose only return_value is "b-neg". Only the .inputs.json sidecars are file-scoped (a.ts/classify.inputs.json, b.ts/classify.inputs.json).
findings.recommendation: Key behavior maps by qualified ID (file-relative path plus function, as scan's str-fuhw work does for callees) and add a regression test with two same-named functions. revalidate should refuse to replay a map whose source file differs from its target.
findings.agent_root_cause: Single-file examples never produce name collisions; no test covers multi-file identity.

In my run the shared map had behaviors: [] (see goals-03) rather than only 'b-neg', so I could not reproduce the exact overwrite content, but the bare-name keying (cache.rs path_for(function_id)) is confirmed.

findings.title: Rust frontend generates negative integers for usize parameters; the deserialization failures appear as behaviors
findings.evidence: goals-runs/rust-walk.md, parse_language_preference: more than 6 rows 'throws runtime_error: input 1 deserialization failed: invalid value: integer `-998`, expected usize' (also -44, -1, -644, -838, i64::MIN).

findings.agent_root_cause: The walkthrough error regex does not match 'deserialization failed' (reported in the prior audit), so these rows never fail a gate.

verify.note: Reproduced with the current release shatter plus shatter-rust: `explore 18_accept_language.rs:parse_language_preference` gave 23 rows, 19 of them 'expected usize' deserialization failures. So this is a regression, or an incomplete fix on this harness path; prior_ref should be str-ddxe, not only str-qwua7.14. Because it may be a regression, it arguably qualifies as P1. I kept P2 because I could not determine which harness mode bypasses the fix.

dedupe.note: str-ddxe (closed) claims usize, u8 and other unsigned ints now generate non-negative values (int_signed on TypeInfo::Int), but the finding shows negative usize inputs still being generated. str-qwua7.14 (open) is the related Rust walkthrough param-type disagreement. str-4yc9w (open, Go) covers the second half: deserialization failures misclassified as target outcomes. str-cfsa (closed) was the Go counterpart.

findings.title: `task --list-all --json` inside the meta stage writes checksums for all 39 tasks, so `task check` and CI skip every stage-2/3 test
findings.evidence: Fresh worktree, no .task at start. `task check` exited 0 after 2472 s, but 13 lines read 'Task "X" is up to date' for rust-rt:test, go:vet, go:test, ts:test, cli:test, rust-fe:test, core:test-ignored, conformance and parity. Reproduced in a git-archive copy: `task --list-all --json` creates .task/checksum with 39 files, while `task --list-all`/`--list` create 0. CI run 35756993223 (task v3.53.1) shows the same up-to-date skips. CI wall time dropped from about 300-650 s to about 185 s after b12e3054 (2026-08-29), which added the test. With .task deleted, running the stages directly exposed a Go test failure, 10 TS timeouts and a core timeout.
findings.recommendation: Run the listing in a copied fixture dir, or set TASK_TEMP_DIR to a tmpdir for that subprocess, or parse Taskfile YAML instead. Add a regression test that runs meta and then asserts that .task/checksum contains no stage-2/3 entries. Make CI run with a pristine .task after meta (e.g. `task --force` per leaf, or TASK_TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)). Implement str-qwua7.2's executed-vs-skipped receipt so a gate fails when a required leaf reports 'up to date' in fresh mode. Consider reporting upstream to go-task.
findings.agent_root_cause: A meta test ran a go-task command against the live repo and assumed a read-only listing has no side effects. No gate checks that required leaves actually executed, so the green CI/check result was trusted for about 3 weeks. The earlier audit (str-qwua7.3) saw the symptom but never tried bisecting which command writes checksums.

verify.note: Reproduced independently in a git-archive copy of HEAD with task 3.50.0: `task --list-all` created 0 checksum files, then `task --list-all --json` created 39 in .task/checksum (core-test-ignored, go-test, ts-test, cli-test, rust-fe-test, conformance, parity and others). scripts/test_affected_gates.py:203-211 runs `task --list-all --json` with cwd=ROOT. It runs inside meta (Taskfile.yml:459), which is a dep of check-static (Taskfile.yml:546) and so runs before check-unit and check-integration. check.log:780-799 and 942 show the 'up to date' lines. b12e3054 is dated 2026-08-29. The recommendations are sound. An isolated TASK_TEMP_DIR is the simplest fix.

dedupe.note: str-qwua7.3 (open) asks why stage-2/3 tasks report 'up to date' right after .task/checksum is deleted, and does not know the cause. This finding supplies the root cause: `task --list-all --json` inside meta rewrites the checksums. Add the root cause, the regression test and the TASK_TEMP_DIR fix to str-qwua7.3, or file a child fix issue under it. str-qwua7.2 (open) already covers the executed-vs-skipped receipt and check-fresh.

findings.title: CI 'Full landing gate' has run no unit, integration, e2e, conformance or parity tests since about 2026-08-29
locations: CLAUDE.md:Code Quality Standards (snapshots verified in CI)
findings.evidence: The CI log for 35756993223 contains 'Task "go:test" is up to date' ... 'Task "core:test-ignored" is up to date', 'Task "conformance" is up to date', 'Task "parity" is up to date'. The only 'test result:' lines in that CI log come from the separate shatter-llm step. The main branch has been merged on green CI throughout this period.

findings.title: go:test fails on main: the Go config loader walks up to / and picks up a stray /tmp/.shatter/config.yaml, and it also rejects the `defaults` key that `shatter init` generates
findings.evidence: 'loader_test.go:668: expected empty File, got {... Warnings:[config /tmp/.shatter/config.yaml: ignoring unknown top-level key "defaults"]}'. /tmp/.shatter/config.yaml was created at 11:40 by an implicit `shatter init` ('Generated by `shatter init`'; top-level `defaults:`). The test passes with TMPDIR=/var/tmp/... The failure reproduces 2 out of 2 times with the default TMPDIR.
findings.recommendation: Make the test hermetic: stop the upward search at a sentinel or VCS root, or inject a search root. Decide on a config-discovery boundary for the product that matches core/TS/Rust behaviour (project or VCS root, not /). Add `defaults` (and any other init-generated keys) to Go's knownTopLevelKeys and add a parity test that loads `shatter init` output in every frontend without warnings. Separately, find which agent or test runs shatter with cwd=/tmp and so implicitly inits there (see str-qwua7.58).
findings.agent_root_cause: Tests use t.TempDir() under the shared /tmp, and the loader's discovery has no ceiling. Implicit init writes into whatever cwd it runs in. The earlier bug report recorded only the symptom.

verify.note: loader.go:228-249 walks up to the filesystem root with no ceiling. knownTopLevelKeys at :417-420 contains only functions and go_runtime_values. /tmp/.shatter/config.yaml exists, reads 'Generated by `shatter init`' and has top-level `defaults:` at line 19. go-test-rerun.log shows the exact failure at loader_test.go:668. str-k7czv is open at P3 and records only the symptom, so this finding adds the root cause and the separate product bug: the Go frontend warns on init-generated `defaults`. P2 is justified because every init-generated config triggers that warning in the Go frontend. I did not re-run with a different TMPDIR.

dedupe.note: str-k7czv (open, P3) records the symptom only: TestLoad_MissingFile_ReturnsZeroFile fails on main, cause unknown. Add the root cause (the upward walk to / picks up /tmp/.shatter/config.yaml) to it. Two parts are new: the Go loader rejects the `defaults` key generated by `shatter init`, and there is no cross-frontend test that loads `shatter init` output. str-qwua7.58 covers implicit init and --no-init, which relates to the cwd=/tmp init source.

findings.title: core:test-ignored sweeps in the bench_frontier_ranking benchmark, which times out, and fail-fast then leaves 87 core tests unrun

findings.title: `task affected` sends docs-only diffs to a hollow `docs` gate and never runs docs-smoke; shatter-llm diffs fall through to `check`, which does not test shatter-llm
findings.evidence: _classify returns {'docs'} for any *.md. The `docs` task is test -f checks plus markdownlint/vale/lychee, all of which print '[skip] ... not installed' (check.log:59-71). docs-smoke validates README/QUICKSTART/SPEC/docs/INDEX against the built CLI but appears in neither GATE_ORDER nor _classify. shatter-llm/ paths are unmatched, so they select `check`, which runs no shatter-llm clippy or tests (CI adds those separately).
findings.recommendation: Map README.md/QUICKSTART.md/SPEC.md/docs/INDEX.md (and scripts/docs-smoke*) to docs-smoke. Make `docs` fail when its linters are missing and CI=1 (str-qwua7.46). Fold shatter-llm into check-static/check-unit (str-35vtk.36) and give it its own affected classification.
findings.agent_root_cause: The diff-scoped selector was written against the task list, with no test asserting that every validator of a path class is selected for that class.

verify.note: affected-gates.py:126-127 maps any *.md or docs/ path to {'docs'} before any per-crate rule. So edits to shatter-ts/CLAUDE.md or shatter-go/CLAUDE.md (the parity contracts) also skip parity and conformance, a further gap the finding does not mention. docs-smoke and shatter-llm do not appear in the script. An unmatched path adds 'check'. The docs task (Taskfile.yml:353-378) is only test -f checks plus linters that print [skip] when missing. The recommendation is sound. Also route frontend CLAUDE.md edits to parity.

findings.title: Gates are slow and unreliable on the shared machine: 16-28% of recorded gate runs fail, and a cold full check takes 40+ minutes under contention
findings.evidence: CSV since 2026-08-10: affected 44/156 non-zero, check-fast 36/151, check 21/135. In this run, workspace clippy alone took 14m48s and 22m01s at load 100-190. Stage-2 alone took 1558 s. gate-wrapper's semaphore only governs shatter gates, not other agents' cargo/jest runs. The median check of 129 s shows most recorded checks were mostly cached no-ops.
findings.recommendation: Record in the receipt CSV whether each leaf ran or was cached, so budgets reflect real work. Share a sccache/CARGO_TARGET_DIR across worktrees (sccache is installed but RUSTC_WRAPPER is unset). Extend the machine-wide slot to run-heavy/bento so cross-project load is also bounded. Recompute gate-budgets.md from real-execution rows only.
findings.agent_root_cause: Governance was designed per project, and timing telemetry does not separate executed runs from cached ones, so slowness and hollowness were both invisible.

verify.note: The recomputed ~/.cache/shatter/gate-times.csv now gives affected 44/156, check-fast 36/151 and check 26/141 non-zero exits (18%), with a check median wall of 149 s (it has grown since the finding). The failure-rate range is roughly right. sccache is installed at /usr/bin/sccache, RUSTC_WRAPPER is unset in env, and .cargo/config has no rustc-wrapper, so that claim is confirmed. The CSV has no executed-vs-cached column, which supports the recommendation. I did not verify the clippy 14m48s/22m01s timings. The claim that the median shows mostly cached no-ops is inference. This overlaps str-35vtk/str-0f6ze and gates-01.

The closed str-35vtk.2 documented a host-level sccache setup and explicitly rejected a shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR. The finding that RUSTC_WRAPPER is unset on this host, and the extension of the machine-wide slot to other projects, are new. The measured 16-28% failure rate is new evidence.
